requirement: generateToolTipFragment(String toolTipText) throws IllegalArgumentException (via the delegate htmlEscape call) when toolTipText is null, rather than producing a fragment containing the literal text 'null'.
PiePlot.getMaximumExplodePercent() returns 0.0 (rather than throwing a NullPointerException by dereferencing the dataset's keys) when the plot's dataset is null.

When the cached bounds are recomputed over all cells, the minimum range bound equals the smallest min-outlier value attained by any stored item and the maximum range bound equals the largest max-outlier value attained by any stored item; stored items whose minOutlier or maxOutlier is null or whose corresponding value is NaN contribute nothing to that extreme (their NaN must not corrupt the cached bounds).

For a horizontal-oriented plot, drawing a data item whose mean value (dataset.getMeanValue(row, column)) is null completes without throwing a NullPointerException: the item returns early, drawing no bar, no standard-deviation/error-indicator lines, and no item label for that item.

After data items are added to a TimePeriodValues series (via add), getMaxMiddleIndex() returns the index of the item whose period's middle instant (= start + (end-start)/2) is the greatest among all held items: adding an item whose middle is less than or equal to the current maximum does not update maxMiddleIndex, even when that item's middle is greater than the current minimum-middle item's middle.

renderWrappedText, when a continuation line of the wrapped text is longer than the configured width and its computed wrap position has fallen back to the end of the leading indentation padding (i.e. wrapping would only split off the padding/prefix column rather than any content), appends the entire remaining text as a final line and returns normally, instead of repeatedly re-splitting at that same padding position.

When a text to be rendered (wrapped) over multiple lines requests a continuation indent nextLineTabStop that is greater than or equal to the total line width, the wrapping process always terminates and produces the full wrapped output, instead of entering the previously unbounded re-wrapping loop that hung indefinitely for inputs such as an option with a run-on description rendered under a narrow total width.
TypeHandler.openFile(String str) returns a FileInputStream opened on the file at the given path when that file exists and can be opened.

TypeHandler.createValue(String, Class<T>) throws a ParseException whose message is "Unable to handle the class: " followed by the string form of the given clazz when clazz matches none of the PatternOptionBuilder sentinel values recognized by the method (STRING_VALUE, OBJECT_VALUE, NUMBER_VALUE, DATE_VALUE, CLASS_VALUE, FILE_VALUE, EXISTING_FILE_VALUE, FILES_VALUE, URL_VALUE), rather than returning null.

When processing a global-scope assignment whose LHS is a tracked name, if that assignment node is the first (callee) child of a CALL node — i.e. the assigned value is used directly as the function being invoked — NameAnalyzer records no dependency scope tying the assignment's subtree to the LHS name. Consequently global names referenced inside that assignment (e.g. within the body of the assigned function being called) are not classified as existing only because the LHS name is referenced, so they remain kept/referenced and are not removed even when the LHS name itself is unreferenced (e.g. in `var fun, x; (fun = function(){ x; })();` the reference to `x` is preserved while the now-unreferenced alias `fun` is removed).

GlobalNamespace's namespace builder treats a NAME node that is the parameter of a CATCH clause (i.e. catch (e) {...}) as a set/redefinition of that name: the reference is recorded as a SET_FROM_GLOBAL set (in global scope) or a SET_FROM_LOCAL set (in a local scope), with the name's type recorded as OTHER, instead of being classified and recorded as a read/get of the name.

In MaybeReachingVariableUse, when the ControlFlowAnalysis output is processed, a CFG node with an outgoing edge labeled Branch.ON_EX (a statement whose execution may be aborted into an exception handler) is treated as 'conditional', so a variable definition (a plain or compound 'x = ...' assignment, a 'var x = ...' initializer, or an assignment to the loop variable of 'for(x in ...)') located inside such a node no longer kills/removes the reaching uses of that variable that were present in the node's input lattice — the reaching uses entering such a node carry through it.

When transforming a BLOCK_COMMENT, IRFactory reports the SUSPICIOUS_COMMENT_WARNING (at the comment's line) if the comment text contains an '@'-annotation whose '@' immediately follows a '*' that itself follows a '/' (i.e., the comment opener), allowing any run of zero or more space/tab characters between the '*' and the '@' — covering compact '/*@name' as well as '/* @name' / '/*\t@name' forms.

When a ternary conditional (?:) expression appears directly in a for(...) init-clause, any `in` operator occurring inside its consequent (true) or alternate (false) operand is printed parenthesized, so the emitted code re-parses to the same ternary AST rather than the `in` being interpreted bare (e.g. as a for-in clause or a top-level relational in that context); ternaries not inside a for-init clause are printed exactly as before (branches in OTHER context).

The DIRECT_EVAL determination inspects the fully cast-unwrapped callee: a CALL whose callee, after removing any wrapping cast node(s), is a name equal to "eval" is annotated DIRECT_EVAL=true (on that inner eval name node); the presence of cast node(s) around an eval callee no longer prevents DIRECT_EVAL from being set.

TokenStream.isJSIdentifier(String s) returns false for any non-null input string that contains at least one character c for which Character.isIdentifierIgnorable(c) returns true, regardless of whether that character is the first character of the string or appears later.

NodeUtil.canBeSideEffected returns false for a FUNCTION node without descending into the function's parameter list or body, so a function-valued node is never considered to-have/can-be-changed-by side effects based on its internal contents; the function must be an anonymous (expression) function and a non-anonymous FUNCTION node fails a Preconditions.checkState(NodeUtil.isAnonymousFunction) assertion (IllegalStateException).

When collapsing a statement body that is a block containing exactly one non-empty child, a child that is a FUNCTION declaration or a DO loop reached through one or more LABEL wrappers is still treated as a FUNCTION/DO, i.e. the braces around the labeled statement are retained rather than stripping to the bare labeled statement. Concretely the generator now emits e.g. `if(e1){A:function goo(){return true}}` from `if(e1)A:function goo(){return true}` and `if(x){A:do foo();while(y)}` from `if(x)A:do{foo()}while(y)` (previously the block would be stripped, producing the labeled FUNCTION/DO without its enclosing braces).

When a function body begins with one or more consecutive inner function declarations, the injected runtime parameter type-check statements are emitted after (following) those leading inner function declarations rather than at the very top of the body, preserving function-declarations-first ordering (e.g. `function f(i){ function g(){} }` with an annotated param `i` normalizes to `function g(){}` first and then the `jscomp.typecheck.checkType(i, ...)` statement).

Compiler.toSource resolves the code-generation charset from the output charset option by name (Charset.forName) whenever that option is set, and uses no charset (ASCII/escaping mode) when the option is unset; consequently, when an output charset that can represent a character (e.g. UTF-8 with non-Latin1 characters) is in effect, that character is emitted literally rather than as a \uXXXX unicode escape.

While collapsing a global name's declaration, the pass only emits separate flattened global variable declarations for the name's object-literal child values and emits stub variable declarations for the name's not-yet-declared (locally-set) child properties when the name's child property names can themselves be collapsed. When the child property names cannot be collapsed, the declaration of a collapsible name is updated without creating such per-child variables or stubs — an object-literal rvalue's keys are left inline in the kept object literal, and no stub vars are inserted for the name's children.

When scanning a candidate function's body for functions it refers to (used to decide inline/removal conflicts), InlineFunctions reports a referenced function name for a NAME that appears in `ID.call(...)` position at any depth of the body, in addition to plain `ID(...)` callee position; the reference even if not appearing as the direct callee NAME child of a CALL node is not missed.

JSType.isInvariant(other) returns true whenever at least one of the two types is the unknown type: under the invariance check the unknown type is treated as invariant (compatible) with any type, so a pair whose one member is unknown is not disqualified on that account.

An input file that parses cleanly (its parse adds no new errors to the compiler error manager) retains its parsed AST even when some earlier input had already reported parse/halting errors; the empty-script (`IR.script()`) dummy fallback no longer triggers merely because of pre-existing errors from other inputs.

In DIRECT inlining mode, a call is refused (NO) when an argument expression itself carries mutable state (may effect mutable state) and its corresponding parameter is referenced at all in the function body—even a single time—because the argument would have to be aliased into a temporary to be safe.

An object literal annotated with @lends whose lent name only becomes resolvable after the literal itself has been visited during traversal (i.e. the literal is not analyzed when first encountered, but only once traversal reaches the root of the statement containing it) must have its lent type resolved correctly and its properties defined onto that lent type, rather than being typed prematurely with an unresolvable/incorrect @lends type.

When the result of an assignment expression is dropped/not needed by its enclosing code (so the assigned value does not escape via that assignment), a variable with only such assignments and a property/element assignment remains removable rather than being flagged as escaped and kept.

The FunctionRewriter pass does not rewrite a function expression that serves as the body of an ES5 get/set member of an object literal (i.e. whose parent is a GET or SET key) into any of the helper factory calls (JSCompiler_get / JSCompiler_set / JSCompiler_returnArg / JSCompiler_identityFn), even when that function body matches the corresponding reducer's pattern (single-return this-property-get, this-property-assign, immutable-value return, or identity); such an object literal is compiled unchanged and no code change (helper insertion or replacement) is reported for it.

When CodeGenerator escapes a string/regexp with no output CharsetEncoder configured (default printing), a character whose code point is exactly 0x7f (DEL, U+007F) is not appended literally: it is instead emitted in its \u hex JavaScript representation (\u007f).

For an unconditional jump node n that is a bare return (RETURN with no operand), a bare break, or a bare continue, whose CFG node has exactly one outgoing control-flow edge of branch type UNCOND, and which has no following sibling statement except optionally a FUNCTION declaration, the pass treats n as a useless (removable) jump exactly when the node control flow would next continue to — computed as n's computed follow — equals the single unconditional CFG destination of n; when they are equal the statement n is eliminated. Here the computed follow is the concrete statement actually flowed into from the CFG follow node after unwrapping block structure: a BLOCK follow with children resolves to its (recursively unwrapped) first child, an empty BLOCK is threaded through to its own follow, and unwrapping stops at the first non-BLOCK node (or null at end of function). A return that has a value operand is never a candidate for this removal.

When CollapseProperties collapses a global property whose single-declaration value is a FUNCTION (handled by updateSimpleDeclaration), and that function's body references `this`, and the function's recording JSDoc (the name's docInfo) is neither a @constructor nor declares a @this type, the compiler reports an UNSAFE_THIS (JSC_UNSAFE_THIS) diagnostic for each such `this` occurrence, labeled with the property's full name.

CheckGlobalThis's lent-function exemption described above fires only when the @lends lend-name ends with '.prototype'; a function that is an object-literal property of an object literal carrying any other @lends annotation (or none, or a lend-name not ending in '.prototype') is still traversed and remains subject to GLOBAL_THIS reporting for its `this` uses as before.

ReferenceCollection.isAssignedOnceInLifetime() returns false when the variable has exactly one assignment (single l-value or initializing declaration as computed by getOneAndOnlyAssignment) but that sole assignment occurs inside a loop body (DO, WHILE, or FOR) within the function scope containing the assignment.

Base64InputStream.read(byte[], int, int), when invoked with a non-null b, valid offset/len, and len > 0, never returns 0 to its caller so long as more input remains to be transformed: whenever processing the buffered chunk yields zero decoded/encoded output bytes yet (because the pending input has not yet formed a complete decoded/encoded group), the method keeps reading and processing further bytes from the wrapped InputStream and returns a positive count only once at least one transformed byte is available, returning -1 only at genuine end-of-stream. Consequently the intermediate 0 that the inner readResults call can produce prior to EOF is never propagated out of this method.

A CaseInsensitiveMap treats non-null keys whose string representations differ only by character case as equal keys (equivalence used by get/put/remove/containsKey and stored-key forms), and this case-insensitive equivalence and the resulting normalized key set remain unchanged when the default Locale is switched to one with different case-mapping rules (e.g. Turkish), rather than following locale-sensitive String.toLowerCase().

SetUniqueList.subList(fromIndex, toIndex) returns a SetUniqueList backed by a separately-allocated uniqueness Set of its own (not the same Set object the outer SetUniqueList uses), so that structural mutations made to the outer SetUniqueList after the subList is created (adding/removing elements outside the view) do not become visible in the returned sublist's membership checks.

ExtendedProperties.put(Object,Object) returns the value that was previously held under the property named by String.valueOf(key) — i.e. the raw user-store value for that key if present, else the value from the defaults (ExtendedProperties 'defaults') map if one is configured, else null.

The serialized form of an UnboundedFifoBuffer written by writeObject now contains an int equal to the length of its internal buffer array (buffer.length), written immediately after the element-count int and before the per-element Object values.

combine(ExtendedProperties) copies into the receiver (this) each entry yielded by props.getKeys(), placing the exact value object retrieved via props.get(key) without any ExtendedProperties value-processing: no backslash-unescaping, comma tokenization, or String→List/Vector conversion is applied to copied values. As a result, after combine, getProperty(key) on the receiver returns a value equivalent to the raw stored value in props (e.g. a String containing multiple consecutive backslashes is preserved unchanged rather than being unescaped again as setProperty's addProperty would do).

When reading a new-format entry whose header c_mode has zero file-type bits (mode & S_IFMT == 0) and whose name is not "TRAILER!!!", CpioArchiveInputStream throws an IOException (message "Mode 0 only allowed in the trailer..."), regardless of whether the mode word itself is exactly zero or merely lacks file-type bits.

Byte production for a decoded block is initiated lazily on the read path rather than during construction: a freshly-constructed stream whose decoder is positioned at START_BLOCK_STATE yields its first decompressed byte on the first read() call (START_BLOCK_STATE is serviced by performing block output setup and returning its byte), rather than having block output set up and a pending byte buffered ahead of time by the constructor.
X7875_NewUnix.getCentralDirectoryLength() returns a ZipShort whose value is 0 regardless of the current UID/GID settings, rather than reporting the same length as getLocalFileDataLength().

TarArchiveEntry.isDirectory() returns false for an entry whose file is null and whose linkFlag is neither LF_DIR nor a PAX/global-PAX extended header flag, is not a directory by other means, even when its name ends in "/"...
UnixStat exposes a new public constant FILE_TYPE_FLAG with the value 0170000 (octal, i.e. 0xF000 / 61440), representing the mask over the 4-bit filesystem-object type indicator within a Unix mode.

ZipArchiveInputStream.canReadEntryData returns false for a ZipArchiveEntry whose compressed size is ArchiveEntry.SIZE_UNKNOWN, unless the entry's compression method tolerates an unknown size, i.e. it is DEFLATED, ENHANCED_DEFLATED, or STORED fired only when the entry uses a data descriptor and allowStoredEntriesWithDataDescriptor is enabled (all other methods with an unknown compressed size now yield false).

In the DEFLATE read path, when the underlying Inflater has completed (inflate returns 0 and inf.finished() is true), read(byte[],int,int) still returns -1, signalling end of the compressed entry, regardless of the state of the underlying stream.

In CSVFormat#printAndQuote's QuoteMode.MINIMAL branch (the effective mode when getQuoteMode() is null) with quoting enabled, when the printed value begins a new record/line (newRecord is true), a value is no longer automatically wrapped in the quote character merely because its leading character is non-alphanumeric; instead such wrapping is forced at a value start only when the leading character is not a legal RFC4180 TEXTDATA printable character (i.e. is a control char < U+0020, is the double-quote U+0022, is the comma U+002C, or is > U+007E) or when the leading character is <= the comment-start character '#'. Consequently a first-column value whose leading character is an ordinary printable punctuation such as '-', '.', '!', '$', '(' or space prints without surrounding quotes when it contains no quote character, delimiter, CR/LF, or trailing-space char that independently forces quoting — e.g. a negative-number value like '-57' in the first column is emitted unquoted.

Each invocation of CSVParser.iterator() on the same parser returns the same single CSVRecordIterator instance (not a newly created iterator), so a caller observing iterator identity sees the identical object across repeated calls.

CSVRecord.putIn (and hence CSVRecord.toMap, which delegates to putIn) no longer throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException / fails when a mapped column's index is not less than the record's value count (values.length); such an out-of-range column is simply skipped, so the produced map contains no entry for that header. Mapped columns whose index is less than values.length are still populated with their header-to-value mapping.

A strict (non-lenient) JsonWriter accepts a call that writes a scalar (non-container) value directly at the root as the document's sole content — via value(...), jsonValue(...), or nullValue() (e.g. writer.value(1), writer.value("hi")) — emitting that value to the output, instead of throwing IllegalStateException "JSON must start with an array or an object."

JsonWriter now provides an overloaded value(Boolean) method: encoding a non-null boxed Boolean writes the JSON literal "true" or "false" to the underlying output, equivalent to value(boolean) with the same truth value.

The single-quad hash function `calcHash(int q1)` re-mixes the intermediate hash after its high/low 16-bit fold: it additionally XORs the running hash with a copy shifted left by 3, then adds the high bits shifted right by 12. For each fixed (seed, q1) input this returns a different int hash value than the prior fold-only formulation, and consequently distributes single-quad (short, ~<=3-character) field names over differently-spread primary/subsequent slots, so that a seed that previously routed a run of small/colliding keys into one slot chain no longer does so.

When a raw-write input does genuinely contain a lone first-pair (high) surrogate with no second-pair element available at end of input, so that _outputRawMultiByteChar reports the 'Split surrogate' failure, the resulting error message now takes the form "Split surrogate on writeRaw() input (last character): first character 0x<hex>" and therefore exposes the UTF-16 code unit of the offending first surrogate (rather than the previous message with no code-unit detail); this is observable in the message of the thrown JsonGenerationException.

When parsing an unquoted field name (Feature.ALLOW_UNQUOTED_FIELD_NAMES enabled) in ReaderBasedJsonParser on the secondary/buffer-continuation path (_handleOddName2), a character whose code-unit value equals the size of the JS-name lookup table `codes` (`codes.length`, 256) is no longer used to index that table; instead it is accepted into the field name if Character.isJavaIdentifierPart(char) is true for it, so that parsing such a name completes normally (no ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException) and yields a FIELD_NAME token containing that character.

When the current node traversed by TreeTraversingParser is a TextNode whose text cannot be decoded under the Base64Variant passed to getBinaryValue(Base64Variant), the method propagates an InvalidFormatException for the broken Base64 content (it does not swallow the decode failure and return null).

When resolving a polymorphic subtype, if class lookup throws an Exception other than ClassNotFoundException, the InvalidTypeIdException whose message is built as "problem: (<exception class>) <text>" embeds, as <text>, the exception's message via ClassUtil.exceptionMessage semantics, so a JsonProcessingException cause contributes its location-less original message.

JdkDeserializers.find(Void.class, ...) — i.e. resolution for the java.lang.Void target type — returns NullifyingDeserializer.instance (a non-null deserializer that discards/nullifies the JSON value to null) instead of returning null, so deserializing into a java.lang.Void type no longer falls through to reflective default construction of Void's private constructor.

Calling CreatorProperty.withValueDeserializer(deser) on a property whose value deserializer and null-value provider are the same object returns a property whose null-value provider is also replaced by `deser` (so the two remain the same object); when the property's null provider is a different object from its value deserializer, the returned property keeps that distinct null provider and replaces only the value deserializer.

MapDeserializer.isCachable() returns false whenever a non-standard (supplied, i.e. non-null) key deserializer is in effect, so that a Map-typed property whose keys are deserialized with a custom key deserializer does not get served by a cached MapDeserializer instance built for another property's context (the custom key deserializer is reapplied per-property rather than being reused across contexts).

ObjectNode.setAll(Map<String,? extends JsonNode>) is excluded (via @JsonIgnore) from Jackson's bean-property introspection, i.e. it is no longer treated as the setter of an introspectable bean property named after the method.

When StringArrayDeserializer deserializes via the custom value-deserializer path (i.e., a non-default String element deserializer is configured, after contextualization), each JSON null element (VALUE_NULL token) of the input array is resolved by invoking that element deserializer's getNullValue(), and the returned value (which may be non-null) is stored as that position of the result array, rather than the position always being Java null.

When StdKeySerializers.EnumKeySerializer serializes an enum key and SerializationFeature.WRITE_ENUMS_USING_TO_STRING is enabled at serialization time, the field name is written as value.toString(), overriding any annotation-derived name; only when that feature is disabled is the introspector-derived/name() value written.

When a ValueInstantiator for a Collection returns true for canCreateUsingArrayDelegate() but getArrayDelegateType(config) returns null, collection deserialization setup aborts by throwing an IllegalArgumentException whose message starts with 'Invalid array-delegate-creator definition for ' and mentions both 'canCreateUsingArrayDelegate()' and 'null for 'getArrayDelegateType()''.

For a POJO whose type/class-level serialization inclusion is NON_DEFAULT (so that 'real' per-property defaults are in effect, per _useRealPropertyDefaults), when that POJO cannot be instantiated as a default bean (e.g. it has no accessible no-arg/default constructor), the affected properties are configured with null suppression, so a property whose value is null is omitted from the JSON output (a null field is not written), exactly as under the general/per-property NON_DEFAULT fallback handling.

When a delegating key deserializer (DelegatingKD) deserializes a Map key, the wrapped delegate JsonDeserializer reads its input from a dedicated parser whose token stream contains exactly that key's text (written as a string value), instead of from the underlying document parser that was in the middle of reading the surrounding JSON.

InnerClassProperty.getCreatorIndex() returns the creator index reported by the wrapped delegate property (the value of _delegate.getCreatorIndex()), so that for a wrapped creator-backed property the index returned is the delegate's non-negative creator index rather than the IllegalStateException that SettableBeanProperty.getCreatorIndex() throws for properties without an assigned creator index.

When EnumSerializer.createContextual computes the property-level serialization decision for an enum object whose property carries a @JsonFormat whose shape does not positively dictate a form (shape absent/unspecified, or Shape.ANY, or Shape.SCALAR), that undetermined shape no longer overrides the serializer's pre-existing static choice: the surviving serializer keeps the prior _serializeAsIndex decision instead of reverting the property to dynamic resolution based on SerializationFeature.WRITE_ENUMS_USING_INDEX.

The JsonMappingException raised for the blocked type identifies the offending class and the reason, formatted as "Illegal type (TemplatesImpl) to deserialize: prevented for security reasons" where the parenthesized token is the actual simple class name of the blocked type.

In CreatorCollector.verifyNonDup, when a creator is being added to a slot whose existing creator has a different explicit status than the new one (one explicitly annotated, the other auto-detected), no conflict/type-selection logic runs and no IllegalArgumentException is thrown regardless of parameter-type overlap: if the existing creator is explicit and the new one is not, the new one is skipped (the existing explicit creator is kept); if the existing creator is auto-detected and the new one is explicit, the new explicit creator replaces/overrides the existing one.

For a ResolvedRecursiveType whose self-reference has been resolved (setReference called), getSuperClass() returns the super class reported by the referenced type (i.e. the getSuperClass() of _referencedType), rather than returning null.

DeserializerCache treats a map-like type whose key type carries a custom value handler as having custom handlers even when the type's content type has no value handler and no type handler; concretely this excludes such a map type from the cached-deserializer store — a cached-entry lookup for it returns null (forcing deserializer reconstruction) and a freshly constructed deserializer for it is not added to the cached-deserializer map, so repeated resolution of such a map type does not reuse a prior installed deserializer.

CharacterReader normalizes its constructor input so that every carriage return, whether part of a CRLF ("
") sequence or a standalone "", is converted to a single line feed ("
"); because the normalized string is stored and used by all read operations (current, consume, matches*, consume*, isEmpty boundaries, toString), every read reflects this normalization — e.g. reading a reader constructed over "12
3" yields content "1
2
3".

In Whitelist URL-attribute protocol validation (method testValidProtocol), when el.absUrl resolves to an empty string (the value could not be made absolute, e.g. unknown/custom scheme with no resolvable base), the attribute's own original value is used as the basis for the allowed-protocol prefix check instead of the empty string, so a link or URL attribute value that cannot be absolutized is not rejected (dropped as unsafe) for that reason alone — it is validated by its as-written value.

org.jsoup.parser.Parser exposes a new public static method parseBodyFragmentRelaxed(String bodyHtml, String baseUri) that parses bodyHtml as HTML into the body of a Document shell (as a body fragment) and returns the parsed Document.

When parsing XML, a bogus comment token whose data begins with `!` (content reached via `<` followed by `!` that is not recognized as a doctype, CDATA section, or regular `<!--...-->` comment, and is longer than one character) is inserted into the document tree as an XmlDeclaration node with nodeName `#declaration`, whose whole-declaration text is the input minus its leading `!`, instead of being inserted as a `#comment` node.

When the tokeniser parses a doctype declaration whose after-name keyword is PUBLIC or SYSTEM (matched case-insensitively), the resulting Token.Doctype records that keyword as the canonical uppercase string "PUBLIC" or "SYSTEM" respectively, and getPubSysKey() returns it; when a doctype declares neither keyword (e.g. bare <!DOCTYPE html>), getPubSysKey() returns null.

Attributes.removeIgnoreCase(String key), when iterating attributes whose keys match key case-insensitively, removes (deletes from the Attributes set) at least one — and each — case-insensitively-matching attribute and completes normally without throwing a ConcurrentModificationException after removing an attribute during the iteration.

Evaluator.MatchText.matches returns true if and only if the candidate element is a PseudoTextElement; for any ordinary element it returns false (and, as described separately, performs a DOM restructuring).

When a consume operation in CharacterReader targets a span with fewer than one character remaining to return (an empty zero-length, or negative-length range at end-of-content), it returns the empty string "" instead of proceeding to construct a String from that (now empty/out-of-range) sub-span of the buffer, which would otherwise trigger a StringIndexOutOfBoundsException. Observable through the cacheString-backed consume methods (e.g. consumeTo(char), consumeToEnd): consuming at/near end-of-content yields "" without throwing.

When the XML parser processes a bogus comment whose data is longer than one character and begins with '!' or '?', and re-parsing the wrapped inner content ("<"+data.substring(1,len-1)+">") as an XML fragment yields a document with zero child nodes (i.e. the content cannot be parsed into an element), XmlTreeBuilder does not attempt to build an XmlDeclaration and does not raise an exception; the node inserted into the tree remains an ordinary Comment carrying the original comment text.

When DataUtil.parseInputStream is given a null charset, finds no BOM and no <meta> charset, and the first child node of the resulting first-pass UTF-8-parsed document is a Comment whose data constitutes an XML declaration (i.e. it passes Comment.isXmlDeclaration) that names 'xml' and carries an 'encoding' attribute — the situation arising when the HTML parser tokenizes a leading <?xml version="..." encoding="X"?> prolog as a Comment rather than directly as an XmlDeclaration — the foundCharset is set from that declaration's encoding attribute, so the full stream is re-decoded using charset X (mirroring the behavior already present when that first child is a genuine XmlDeclaration). Observable upshot: e.g. Jsoup.parse(stream of bytes in iso-8859-1 beginning with <?xml version="1.0" encoding="iso-8859-1"?>, null, uri) yields a Document whose text content is decoded with iso-8859-1 rather than the default charset.

Comment.asXmlDeclaration() constructs an XmlDeclaration only when re-parsing the comment data (with data's first and last characters stripped and wrapped as '<...>') using the XML parser yields a Document that has at least one child ELEMENT (as reported by Element.children()); when the re-parsed Document has no element child (i.e. contains only non-element child nodes such as text/comment/data nodes, or is empty), asXmlDeclaration() returns null and the comment is left as a plain Comment (rendered as <!--data-->) rather than being turned into a mis-formed XML declaration.

Constructing a CharacterReader (via any of its constructors, since all delegate to CharacterReader(Reader, int) after the initial buffer-up) over input whose initially-buffered content contains 10 or more NUL ('\0') characters throws an UncheckedIOException with message "Input is binary and unsupported".

DOMNodePointer.getNamespaceURI(Node node) returns null (rather than the empty string) whenever the resolved namespace URI for the node is the empty string — whether resolved via element.getNamespaceURI() or, when that returns null, via the nearest xmlns/xmlns:prefix attribute declaration found while walking up from the node through its enclosing elements.

NullPropertyPointer.createPath(context), in the non-attribute case, throws a JXPathAbstractFactoryException when the parent pointer is a NullPointer whose createPath returns a NullPointer equal to the original parent (i.e. the factory reported success but produced no distinct/null-realized object), instead of proceeding to delegate to newParent.createChild (which would recurse indefinitely).

FastDateFormat.format(Date date) builds its calendar with the formatter's configured locale (mLocale), so that for patterns containing locale-sensitive numeric calendar fields whose computation depends on the calendar's first-day-of-week / minimal-days-in-first-week conventions (e.g. week-of-year from the 'w' rule and week-of-month from the 'W' rule), the output for a given Date reflects the formatter's locale's conventions rather than those of the JVM default locale.

NumberUtils.createNumber rejects as invalid any input containing a '.' in which the exponent-marker position expPos (= str.indexOf('e') + str.indexOf('E') + 1) falls after the decimal point but exceeds the string's length (so expPos is not before decPos yet still past the end) by throwing NumberFormatException with message str + " is not a valid number." rather than throwing StringIndexOutOfBoundsException from str.substring(decPos+1, expPos).

NumberUtils.isNumber returns true for a string whose final character is a '.' that is the only decimal point (no earlier '.' and no exponent) and is preceded by at least one digit, e.g. isNumber("2.") == true.

ClassUtils.getShortClassName decodes primitive-array component abbreviations: after stripping the leading '[' dimensions, if the remaining element is a JVM primitive abbreviation present in the reverse abbreviation map (one of I,Z,F,J,S,B,D,C), it is expanded to its primitive name and one '[]' is suffixed per dimension. E.g. getShortClassName("[I") == "int[]" and getShortClassName(int[].class) == "int[]". This reverse-abbreviation decode also applies to a directly-passed bare abbreviated name (e.g. getShortClassName("I") == "int") since it is applied to the className unconditionally.
escapeJava(Writer, String) writes a forward-slash character to the Writer as a bare '/' and does not emit a preceding backslash for it.

escapeJava(String) and escapeJava(Writer,String) escape each literal forward-slash character '/' in the printable-ASCII position of the input by writing the two characters backslash then slash ("\/") rather than outputting the slash bare (the new case is not gated on the escape-SingleQuote flag).

StrBuilder.indexOf(String str, int startIndex) bounds its forward scan using the builder's current logical size rather than the possibly-larger backing-array capacity: it only considers candidate start positions i for which the whole str would fit within the current content (i.e. it stops searching at size - strLen + 1). Consequently, whenever the internal character array has unused/stale slots beyond the current logical content (which arises naturally after the content shrinks, e.g. via deleteAll/deleteFirst/replace), the method returns -1 instead of returning a match index that lies at or past the current content end, and the deleteAll(String)/deleteFirst(String)/replaceAll(String,String)/replaceFirst(String,String)/contains(String) flows built on this indexOf no longer act on (or copy from) beyond-current-content positions.

guessParametersErrors throws an EstimationException for insufficient degrees of freedom (message reporting the parameter count) if and only if the number of measurements is less than or equal to the number of unbound parameters of the problem.

The NumberIsTooLargeException thrown by the boundary range-overflow guard reports the overflowing upper-bound value with an OVERFLOW message in its exception context and an INDEX message identifying the coordinate (dimension) whose upper−lower range overflowed.

In each reduction step of the pivoted rectangular Cholesky construction, the column selected for the next elimination is the remaining column with the largest current working-matrix diagonal element (correct maximal-element column pivoting). Concretely, the decomposition of the full-rank order-4 symmetric positive semidefinite covariance matrix reported in the issue (MATH-789 m1, threshold 1.0e-10) yields a root B with ||B·B^T − M|| at/near machine precision (~1e-16), instead of one corrupted by pivoting on a stale, out-of-date diagonal entry.

When an optimization terminates because the user-supplied ConvergenceChecker reports convergence during doOptimize, the returned point (result of optimize) is the better of the two most recently evaluated points (`current` and `previous`) according to the goal type — the one with the lower objective value when the goal is MINIMIZE, and the higher when the goal is MAXIMIZE — rather than unconditionally the most recently evaluated/latest point.

For the double-to-Fraction continued-fraction conversion, if the magnitude of the integer part `floor(value)` exceeds Integer.MAX_VALUE (in particular for large-magnitude negative values such that floor(value) < -Integer.MAX_VALUE), a FractionConversionException(value, floor(value), 1) is thrown before the near-integer shortcut and before the iteration loop, rather than the conversion continuing and truncating out-of-range values into an incorrect int.

When, during acceptance of one integrator step that had multiple event handlers scheduled to occur (pending) inside it, the chronologically-first event's handler requests STOP so that acceptStep copies its interpolated state into y and returns that event's time early having marked the step as last, every other event handler that was also scheduled to occur later within the same candidate step is notified via stepAccepted at that same event time (with the copied state) before acceptStep returns, so none of the remaining handlers is left stepping from stale (pre-event) bracketing state.

RegulaFalsiSolver (BaseSecantSolver.doSolve with method==REGULA_FALSI) never performs an objective-function evaluation at an interior anti-stagnation point: computeObjectiveValue is invoked only at the two initial bounds and at each successive Secant approximation x, never additionally from within the REGULA_FALSI update case, so the total evaluation count for a regula-falsi run is always 2 (bounds) + number of Secant iterations regardless of stagnation.

When a Regula Falsi solver (Method.REGULA_FALSI) reaches an iteration in which the computed secant approximation coincides with the current upper endpoint x == x1 (so the plain false-position update would make no progress), the solver displaces the lower endpoint x0 inward toward x1 (to a point inside [x0, x1]) and recomputes the function value there, so the bracket shrinks and the iteration can continue; consequently a regula falsi solve does not stall indefinitely with the endpoint x1 fixed and, given bracketing and sufficient evaluations, converges to the root rather than cycling or exhausting the evaluation budget at a repeat of x1.

When the input x deviates from the distribution mean by more than 40 times the standard deviation (i.e. |x - mean| > 40 * sd), cumulativeProbability saturates: it returns exactly 0.0 when x < mean and exactly 1.0 when x > mean, and does not invoke Erf for such inputs (so it never throws a MaxIterationsExceededException or other MathException from the erf computation for these extreme inputs).

A freshly constructed LevenbergMarquardtOptimizer has its vectorial convergence checker set to null (overriding the non-null SimpleVectorialValueChecker that the AbstractLeastSquaresOptimizer superclass installs by default), so getConvergenceChecker() returns null after construction unless a checker is explicitly installed afterwards.

For an m×n input matrix with m<n whose compact/truncated SVD retains a positive-singular-value count p strictly less than m (rank deficiency or explicit truncation via constructor max), getV() returns an n×p right-singular factor computed from the full m-row eigenvector submatrix, so that when no truncation was applied the product getU()*getS()*getVT() recomposes the original matrix to within floating-point tolerance (instead of the last retained V column being computed without its secondary-bidiagonal coupling term and thereby causing the recomposition to diverge from the input).

MathUtils.distance(int[] p1, int[] p2) computes the L2 (Euclidean) distance using floating-point (double) accumulation of the per-coordinate squared differences, so that for any two int-coordinate arrays it returns an accurate, finite non-NaN result even when the coordinate differences are large enough that the intermediate sum of squared differences exceeds the range of a 32-bit signed int (i.e., the result is no longer corrupted by integer wraparound of the accumulator).

For symmetric tridiagonal matrices whose dqd iteration reaches the post-ping check on a block segment longer than three rows, a further split is now inserted whenever either the processed diagonal element (work[i+3]) is within the squared-tolerance factor of its current diagonal (work[i]) OR the corresponding off-diagonal element (work[i+2]) is within that factor of the current shift sigma (logical OR), rather than only when both hold; this changes where the qd array is partitioned into independently-dqds'd sub-segments, making the dqd/dqds deflation of such blocks yield a valid, in-range decomposition instead of failing/over-running.

Constructing a CholeskyDecompositionImpl on a symmetric matrix now throws NotPositiveDefiniteMatrixException whenever the matrix is not positive definite as judged by the positivity threshold evaluated on the diagonal pivots during the Cholesky elimination — in particular, symmetric matrices whose original diagonal entries are all above the threshold but whose an updated elimination pivot (at any step) drops below the threshold (e.g. a non-SPD/non-semi-definite matrix for which a pivot becomes negative) are rejected instead of being silently decomposed into matrices containing NaN pivots.

Line.revert() returns a Line whose point closest to the origin (getOrigin()/zero) is unchanged from the receiver's — the reverted line lies on the same geometric line and reverses only the orientation, preserving the receiver's closest-to-origin point exactly rather than recomputing it.

For 0 <= n <= 20 MathUtils.factorialLog(n) returns the natural logarithm of the exact factorial (equal to Math.log of the exact n! value), rather than a value obtained by summing individual Math.log terms.

MockitoCore.mock(Class, MockSettings, boolean shouldResetOngoingStubbing) now performs the reset of the in-progress ongoing-stubbing session on the mocking progress only when shouldResetOngoingStubbing is true; when the flag is false the mock is created without disturbing a current ongoing-stubbing session, so that a subsequent when()/stub() step (e.g. stubbing that was already in progress) can still be completed rather than being wiped out.

ReturnsEmptyValues.returnValueFor(Iterable.class) (and therefore the default Answer for a mocked method whose declared return type is exactly Iterable) returns a newly created empty ArrayList rather than null, so the returned value is non-null, empty, and modifiable (no UnsupportedOperationException when code under test mutates it).

When SpyAnnotationEngine.process encounters a @Spy-annotated field whose value is a non-null instance that is not already a mock, it replaces the field value with a Mockito mock whose configured mock name is the field's own name, so that the created spy is referred to by that field name (e.g. in Mockito error/verification messages that print the mock's name) rather than by a generated default mock name.

In comparing an argument against a matcher's string description (the toStringEquals path used for suspicious-argument detection), a null argument does not throw a NullPointerException: the null argument is treated as having the string representation "null", so a matcher whose StringDescription is the literal string "null" is considered to have an equal string representation.
UnsupportedDurationField.compareTo(DurationField) returns 0 for any argument, whether or not the argument field is supported (it no longer returns 1 when the argument is supported).

BaseSingleFieldPeriod.between(start, end, zeroInstance), as surfaced through concrete single-field period subclasses (e.g. Days.between / Months.between over LocalDate, YearMonth-like, MonthDay-like, MonthDayYear-like partials), returns the correct whole-unit difference between the two partials by resolving both the start and the end partial to instants against the START_1972 reference base instants (chronological ~1972-01-01 each), instead of against the chronological zero instant (ISO epoch 1970-01-01). Consequently it returns the correct count for partial pairs whose resolution against the 1970-epoch base would otherwise produce an off-by-one (dates/crossings near or spanning the epoch/leap boundary), whereas the pre-fix method returned an incorrect count for such inputs.

When computeMillis is invoked with resetFields=true on a bucket holding two or more saved fields, the returned instant is computed so that, after the saved fields have been applied in priority (sorted) order with round-floor resetting, they are applied a second time with reset/round-floor applied only to the last (highest-priority/smallest) saved field; consequently any finer field detail that an intermediate applied field's round-floor in the first pass would otherwise have discarded above the last field is recovered, so the returned millis reflects all saved field values consistently. (With resetFields=false, or a single saved field, the re-pass leaves the result unchanged.)
MutableDateTime.addWeekyears(0) leaves the instant (getMillis) unchanged, i.e. adding zero weekyears is an observable no-op.

When Partial.with(DateTimeFieldType, int) is called with a field type not already present in the partial (the add-new-field branch), the new Partial is constructed via the fully-validating public constructor Partial(DateTimeFieldType[], int[], Chronology), so that any resulting field-type arrangement that violates the Partial invariants (field types not in strictly largest-to-smallest order, or containing an ordering/duplicate conflict) causes an IllegalArgumentException to be thrown — never silently returning a Partial whose internal field-type ordering is invalid.

When the target PeriodType supports months but not years (e.g. PeriodType.months()), normalizedStandard folds the entire combined year+month amount (including whatever years the period holds) into the months field and returns that result without raising an exception. Examples: 1 year 15 months normalizes to 27 months; -2 years 15 months normalizes to -9 months.

GJChronology.getInstance(zone, gregorianCutover, minDaysInFirstWeek) throws IllegalArgumentException when a non-null gregorianCutover resolves (in the target time zone, interpreted on the Gregorian calendar) to a date whose proleptic year is <= 0 — i.e. a cutover on or before 0001-01-01, such as LocalDate(-2,6,30) — so that no GJ chronology can be created whose cutover falls at or before Gregorian year zero. (Calling with a null cutover, which selects the default 1582 cutover, is unaffected.)

For a collection requirement string whose parsed URL scheme is a non-empty value other than http/https (case-insensitive), _get_collection_info does NOT attempt a download; it takes the collection-name path instead (validating the name as a collection name).

The galaxy api module imports a urlparse callable that works on both Python 2 and Python 3, so that lib/ansible/galaxy/api.py imports successfully regardless of interpreter version (falling back from urllib.parse to urlparse).

When the Debian parser recognizes Kali (including from /etc/os-release content), it sets distribution_release to the value captured by the DISTRIB_RELEASE= line of the parsed data whenever such a line is present.
The `collections` FieldAttribute of CollectionSearch is marked as a static attribute, so it is never templated during post-validation; the value is used as-is.

get_future_imports returns the original (unaliased) module name for a future import written with a single `as` alias, e.g. `from __future__ import unicode_literals as _unicode_literals` yields a set containing `"unicode_literals"` (and not `"_unicode_literals"`), rather than raising/asserting.
prepare_input(src: bytes) exists as a module-level function and returns a 3-tuple of (newline, encoding, decoded_contents).

EmptyLineTracker.maybe_empty_lines returns 0 blank lines before a decorator line when the immediately preceding emitted line is a standalone comment line (i.e., a line consisting of a single STANDALONE_COMMENT leaf), regardless of the decorator's indentation depth.

When the platform default encoding differs from UTF-8, the temporary log file produced by black.dump_to_file contains the dumped text encoded as UTF-8 bytes rather than in the platform default encoding.

blib2to3.pygram exports a module-level grammar object named python_grammar_no_print_statement_no_exec_statement that is a copy of python_grammar with both 'print' and 'exec' removed from its keywords.

EmptyLineTracker.maybe_empty_lines returns a `before` count of 0 for the first line it is asked about (i.e. when it has not yet processed any line, so `previous_line is None`), so no empty lines are emitted at the beginning of the formatted file even if the newline count of the first line's first leaf prefix (or any other part of the computation) would otherwise yield a positive count.

The decision to wrap the first testlist_star_expr child in invisible parentheses is triggered by the child's position (index 0) and node type, independent of whether the previous leaf's value was in parens_after, so a statement like `a, b = ...` (with no preceding assignment leaf marker) still gets its tuple target wrapped.

find_hook returns a list of absolute paths to ALL valid hook scripts matching the requested hook name (e.g. both pre_gen_project.py and pre_gen_project.sh are included when both exist), rather than only the first match.
read_user_choice invokes click.prompt with show_choices=False (in addition to the prompt text, type=click.Choice(choices), and default='1').

SchemaBase.additionalProperties no longer accepts values that are neither a boolean nor a mapping (e.g. a bare string, number, or list); such values fail validation instead of being passed through unconstrained as before (the previous Union[bool, Any] allowed any value).

Constructing an APIWebSocketRoute / registering a websocket route continues to succeed with no dependency_overrides_provider configured (the provider defaults to None), and the endpoint still calls the websocket endpoint function with the solved dependency values.

_prepare_response_content recurses into list values, returning a new list in which each element has been prepared, so BaseModels nested inside a list response are also converted (with aliases / exclude_unset applied) rather than being passed through as model instances.

When multiple collected parameters share the same name, the entry kept is the last one encountered in the collected parameter order (its 'in', 'required', 'schema', 'description' and 'deprecated' fields win), rather than the first.

When a form (FormData) body is received, a non-body-typed Form parameter whose declared type is a plain (non-parametrized) sequence type — `list`, `set` or `tuple` — is populated with ALL submitted values for that parameter's alias, so a request sending the same field name multiple times yields every value rather than one single value.

request_validation_exception_handler builds its 422 response content by passing the error list from `exc.errors()` through `jsonable_encoder`, so the emitted JSON body is an encoding of that error list rather than the raw error list.

In Model.fit_generator, when validation_data is a keras.utils.Sequence and validation is run without worker processes (workers == 0), an explicitly supplied truthy validation_steps value is preserved unchanged and is not overridden by len(validation_data).

Sequential.get_config() includes a 'build_input_shape' entry equal to the input_shape value that was passed to build() when the model was built from an explicit shape, and omits the 'build_input_shape' entry entirely when no such shape was ever recorded (e.g. a freshly constructed model, or one built only via a first-layer batch_input_shape).
keras.backend.numpy_backend defines a public module-level function in_top_k(predictions, targets, k) (previously absent from the numpy backend).
Model.compile creates and initializes the attribute self.stateful_metric_functions to an empty list during compilation.
For a None/empty-input batch, fit_generator reports the callback batch log entry 'size' as 1 (the step-size used for data tensors).

ctc_batch_cost preserves the per-sample (batch) dimension of label_length when squeezing: a label_length input of shape (samples, 1) yields a tensor of shape (samples,), including when samples == 1 (i.e. it does not collapse to a scalar when the batch dimension happens to have size 1).
keras.utils.data_utils.Sequence instances are iterable: iterating a Sequence yields its batches via __getitem__ in index order, i.e. self[0], self[1], ..., self[len(self)-1].

ImageDataGenerator.standardize no longer applies the generator's preprocessing_function to its input; standardize only performs rescaling/normalization (rescale, samplewise/featurewise center and std normalization, zca whitening) on the input it is given.

RNN.__call__ decides whether each of the tensors it appends as additional inputs (initial_state and constants) is a Keras tensor by using K.is_keras_tensor rather than checking for a `_keras_history` attribute, and raises ValueError when the additional inputs contain a mix of Keras and non-Keras tensors.

KerasRegressor.predict still forwards kwargs filtered through filter_sk_params(Sequential.predict) to self.model.predict, and its return value remains a numpy array (not a list) of the model's predictions.

MetricsHandler.get invokes configure_http_handler on the metrics collector object (the value of self._scheduler._state._metrics_collector) passing the handler itself, rather than invoking it on the object returned by generate_latest().
The scheduler config parameter `disable_hard_timeout` defaults to 999999999 (rather than None) when not supplied via kwargs or config.

CentralPlannerScheduler.prune() invokes SimpleTaskState.prune on every active task on each call, regardless of whether the task is in necessary_tasks, so prune's state side effects (FAILED->PENDING retry reset when retry delay has elapsed, DISABLED re-enable when disable_persist has elapsed, and stamping task.remove when a task has no stakeholders) are applied to necessary tasks too.
luigi.interface.run called without an explicit cmdline_args argument (cmdline_args is None) does not raise an error and instead proceeds using sys.argv[1:] as the command-line arguments.

S3CopyToTable.run() binds its local load path to the value of the s3_load_path attribute itself (via attribute access that does not invoke it as a callable), rather than to the result of calling s3_load_path.

For an assistant calling get_work, RUNNING tasks whose capable-worker set is empty are excluded from the returned reply's 'running_tasks' list; RUNNING tasks with at least one capable worker remain included.

After applying inherits(TaskA) to a task class, instances of the decorated class expose a callable clone_parent method that returns self.clone(cls=TaskA, **args) with any passed keyword arguments forwarded.

While a task's status is RUNNING or BATCH_RUNNING, a status update to DONE, FAILED, or RUNNING is applied only when the requesting worker equals the task's worker_running; in that case the task's status is updated (and the task history is written).

nonsingular computes its interval/expansion logic on the endpoints' true numeric magnitudes rather than the input integer dtype, so that for integer inputs at the limits of their type (where abs() would wrap around, e.g. numpy int8 -128, or vmax - vmin would overflow) it returns the correct expanded float interval instead of a value derived from wrapped/overflowed intermediates.

DataFrame.append builds the row frame for an appended Series/dict using the index label Index([other.name], name=self.index.name) unconditionally, so the appended row's label is the Series name and the resulting frame's index name is self.index.name (rather than a default/unnamed index).

In _make_concat_multiindex (the branch taken when the passed indexes are not all identical), when a key from a level of `keys` does not occur in the corresponding `level`, the function raises ValueError with the message f"Key {key} not in level {level}" rather than letting a KeyError escape.

A float scalar .loc key on a CategoricalIndex whose categories are string/unicode/mixed is not rejected with a TypeError at the scalar-conversion step; the float key is passed through and the subsequent lookup of an absent label raises KeyError.
IntegerArray ordering comparisons (__lt__, __le__, __gt__, __ge__) against an operand of an incompatible type raise TypeError rather than returning a scalar/incorrect result.

For the non-scipy interpolation path of missing.interpolate_1d (method in {'linear', 'time', 'index', 'values'}), when the x-axis / index values are not monotonically increasing, the interpolated result is nonetheless the value defined by the valid (x, y) pairs treated as a sorted set of knots, rather than the (incorrect) result of passing the unsorted x-knots directly to np.interp. I.e. the each interpolated point equals the linear interpolation between the two valid x-knots that bracket it in sorted order, using the y-value belonging to each of those x-knots.

DataFrame.corr (all methods) operates on a float64 NumPy representation of the numeric-only columns obtained via DataFrame.astype(float, copy=False) followed by to_numpy(), so nullable/extension-array numeric columns (e.g. Int64Dtype with pd.NA) are accepted without raising a conversion error.

When several rows of the intermediate percentage-change result share the same index label, NDFrame.pct_change keeps the first such row for that label and discards the later ones (rather than raising or keeping all of them).

NDFrame.interpolate raises ValueError (the 'No axis named ... for object type ...' error from _get_axis_number) when axis is not a valid axis for the object — e.g. axis=None, axis=2, or an unknown label — instead of failing with a Python unbound-local/NameError.

Categorical.astype(dtype) where dtype is an extension-array dtype (i.e. is_extension_array_dtype(dtype) is True, and dtype is not categorical) returns a pandas array object whose dtype is exactly the requested extension dtype (e.g. an IntervalArray for IntervalDtype), holding the categorical's values in the categorical's order; it no longer falls through to np.array(self, dtype=dtype, copy=copy) and therefore no longer raises 'TypeError: data type not understood' for such dtypes.
_coerce_to_type casts boolean-dtype input to int64, so that boolean data reaching cut/qcut is treated as numeric 0/1 data instead of a bool array.

When array_equivalent is called with strict_nan=True on object/string arrays and element-wise comparison raises a TypeError whose message contains "Cannot compare tz-naive", array_equivalent returns False (treats the arrays as not equivalent) instead of letting the TypeError propagate.

The TypeError raised by DatetimeTZDtype.construct_from_string for a matched-but-unconstructible string chains the underlying construction error as its __cause__ (err.__cause__ is the original KeyError/pytz.UnknownTimeZoneError, TypeError, or ValueError), rather than discarding it.
In apply_empty_result, the reduction-inference probe invokes the apply function with exactly one argument, an empty Series (Series([])), and no additional positional or keyword arguments.

PandasArray.__setitem__(key, value) writes the value into the existing backing ndarray without changing the array's dtype: after any successful assignment self.dtype (and self._dtype) equals the dtype it had before the assignment; no upcasting to a wider result dtype occurs.
Rolling._on returns None (implicit fall-through, no return statement executed) when `on` is None and self.axis is neither 0 nor 1 (e.g. axis=None); previously it returned self.obj.index in that case.

For an operand that exposes a scalar `dtype` attribute (a numpy ndarray or a 1-D Series), _can_use_numexpr includes that operand's dtype name in the set of dtypes considered for the numexpr dtype-compatibility check, so that such an operand's dtype can cause the check to return False when the dtype is not in _ALLOWED_DTYPES[dtype_check].

For the empty-column-collection early return of DataFrame.quantile, the empty Index used for the result's column axis (the Series' index, or the DataFrame's columns) carries the name of the calling frame's columns axis, i.e. self.columns.name, and the result's axis labels are otherwise empty.

MonthOffset.apply_index returns a DatetimeIndex constructed from the shifted i8 values without passing the input index's freq (i.e. the input `i.freq` is not forwarded to `_simple_new`); only `dtype` is forwarded.

IntervalArray.__setitem__ raises a ValueError with the message "Cannot set float NaN to integer-backed IntervalArray" when assigning a scalar NA value (e.g. np.nan, None) to an IntervalArray whose subtype is integer (int*/uint*), and leaves the array unmodified in that case.
The array returned by StringArray.astype to an integer extension dtype is an independent copy: mutating it does not mutate the source StringArray (and vice versa).
ExtensionBlock.set no longer accepts a `check` keyword argument (the signature is set(self, locs, values)).

Assigning via .loc with a label indexer whose column part is a list-like containing labels not present in the columns, e.g. df.loc[:, ['a', 'newcol']] = values, no longer raises for the missing labels: the missing labels are first created as NaN-filled columns, and the assignment then proceeds normally.

In DataFrameGroupBy._cython_agg_blocks, when a block is an extension-dtype block and the aggregated result is an ndarray, if re-casting the result via type(block.values)._from_sequence(result.ravel(), dtype=block.values.dtype) raises a ValueError, the exception is swallowed and the result is instead reshaped to (1, -1) so it is a valid input for a non-Extension Block.

When a CategoricalIndex is joined (Index.join via _join_monotonic or _join_non_unique) and the joined index is wrapped, the result is a CategoricalIndex whose dtype equals the calling index's dtype (same categories and orderedness), instead of a generic Index built from the raw joined values.
For a Series with a string ('abc') object index, ser.at[0] and ser.loc[0] raise KeyError matching '^0$' rather than a TypeError about label indexing.

For a DataFrame with a non-unique info axis (duplicate columns), accessing an item by positional index via NDFrame._iget_item_cache returns the item at that position (through positional item slicing) instead of going through the take-with-is_copy path; the returned object is the column/Series at that integer position.

When a non-scalar aggregation result is cast back to the calling column's extension-array dtype, the cast-back is performed only if the result is non-empty and its first element is an instance of the extension dtype's scalar type; otherwise the result is returned unchanged with its naturally inferred dtype instead of being converted to the extension array type.
Constructing a TimedeltaIndex from an existing TimedeltaArray with freq=None (the default) returns an index whose freq equals the input TimedeltaArray's freq, preserving the fast-path behavior.

Because _convert_axes routes index/column axis data through the same _try_convert_data helper, reading a JSON document whose axis labels require an int64 coercion that overflows also returns a result instead of raising OverflowError.

_get_empty_dtype_and_na returns, for the datetime upcast class, the NA value np.datetime64("NaT", "ns") (a datetime64[ns] scalar) rather than the integer iNaT sentinel, together with the dtype np.dtype("M8[ns]").
The TypeError raised by pivot() for a missing/None `columns` argument has the message "pivot() missing 1 required argument: 'columns'".
to_pickle accepts a generic filepath-or-buffer argument (str path, path-like object, URL, or file-like buffer) named filepath_or_buffer instead of requiring a plain path, resolving it before opening.

The TypeError raised by TimedeltaIndex.searchsorted for an incompatible value carries the message "searchsorted requires compatible dtype or scalar, not {type(value).__name__}" (the offending value's type name is interpolated).

PeriodIndex.searchsorted raises TypeError with a message containing "requires either a Period or PeriodArray" for any argument that is not a Period, NaT, str, or PeriodArray (e.g. an int64 ndarray, a timedelta64 array, a timedelta64 scalar, a datetime64 scalar).

When the uri resolved by the router for the requested view name contains a "/" at a position greater than 0, url_for treats the substring preceding that first "/" as the route's host and removes it from the path, so the produced URL's path portion does not start with the host (e.g. a route uri of "example.com/foo" yields a URL whose path is "/foo").

The ValueError message is exactly '<ClassName>.__init__() received both response and text', where <ClassName> is the runtime class whose __init__ was invoked (subclass-aware, e.g. 'Selector' for Selector and the subclass name for a subclass).

When FormRequest.from_response is called without an explicit url and the form has no 'action' attribute, the resulting request URL is the form's base URL resolved against the document base URL (i.e. the response URL, or the page's <base href> if present), rather than the raw action attribute.

In RedirectMiddleware.process_response, when the raw Location header value starts with '//' (a protocol-relative reference), the redirect target is resolved against the scheme of request.url rather than left to plain relative resolution: the Location value is rewritten to '<scheme-of-request.url>://<Location value with its leading slashes stripped>' before being urljoin-ed with request.url. Thus a request to 'http://example.com/a' with 'Location: //foo.com/path' redirects to 'http://foo.com/path', and an https request yields an 'https://...' target.
When the namespace passed to ItemMeta.__new__ does not contain '__classcell__' (classcell is None), no '__classcell__' key is added to the namespace of the constructed class.
MailSender.send with cc=None does not set a Cc header and adds no cc recipients, i.e. a null cc is treated as an empty address collection rather than as a one-element collection.
The Errors class exposes a new attribute E171 whose value is the message template "Matcher.add received invalid on_match callback argument: expected callable or None, but got: {arg_type}".

The per-component configuration passed to the non-.pipe component in Language.evaluate is the component's entry from component_cfg, with batch_size defaulted to the evaluate batch_size argument, i.e. identical to the kwargs used for the .pipe branch.

spacy.errors.Warnings.W022 can be resolved (no AttributeError) and, through the @add_codes wrapper, resolves to the warning message '[W022] Training a new part-of-speech tagger using a model with no lemmatization rules or data. This means that the trained model may not be able to lemmatize correctly. If this is intentional or the language you're using doesn't have lemmatization data, you can ignore this warning by setting SPACY_WARNING_IGNORE=W022. If this is surprising, make sure you have the spacy-lookups-data package installed.'

In pip_unknown_command.get_new_command, the suggested command name is extracted from output text matching `maybe you meant "..."` by taking the entire quoted token (any characters except a double quote), so a suggestion containing non-[a-z] characters is captured in full rather than only its leading [a-z] prefix.

When get_new_command is called for a `man` command whose script contains neither '2' nor '3' and whose stderr does not indicate a missing manual entry, it returns a three-element list ordered as [man-3 variant, man-2 variant, last_arg + ' --help'], i.e. the last_arg --help suggestion comes last rather than first.

Fish._get_overridden_aliases() returns a set of alias names (a Python set, not a list), so its result compares equal to a set literal of the same names and supports set semantics (e.g. `isinstance`/`type` check reports set).

CorrectedCommand.run(old_cmd) logs the value of the PYTHONIOENCODING environment variable at debug level, using the literal placeholder `!!not-set!!` in place of the value when PYTHONIOENCODING is not present in the environment (when it is set, the actual value is logged).
Bash.get_aliases() returns an empty dict (rather than raising KeyError) when TF_SHELL_ALIASES is not set in the environment.

get_all_executables splits the PATH environment variable using os.pathsep as the directory separator (rather than a hard-coded ':'), so on a platform whose os.pathsep is not ':' (e.g. Windows, where it is ';') a PATH value like 'C:\a;C:\b' is treated as two directory entries and the executables found in both directories are returned (instead of treating the whole string as one non-existent directory path).

Iterating, calling len() on, or indexing (with any index, including out-of-range) a SortedCorrectedCommandsSequence constructed over an empty iterable completes without raising an exception, and iterating/len() report an empty result (list(seq) == [], len(seq) == 0).

fix_file.get_new_command accepts settings that provide the customizable keys `fixlinecmd` and `fixcolcmd`, defaulting to `'{editor} {file} +{line}'` and `None` respectively when the caller does not supply them.
fix_file.match returns a falsy value when a pattern matches the stderr but the matched 'file' group does not name a path that exists as a file on the filesystem (os.path.isfile is false).

get_new_command produces its result by replacing the first occurrence of ' diff' in the script with ' diff --staged', so only the 'diff' token of the git subcommand (and any argument text) is preserved verbatim while the flag is placed after the diff token.

thefuck.rules.php_s.get_new_command returns the command's script with the `-s` argument replaced by `-S`, leaving the remaining arguments intact (e.g. 'php -t pub -s 0.0.0.0:8080' -> 'php -t pub -S 0.0.0.0:8080').

HTTP1Connection._can_keep_alive does not raise AttributeError when start_line is a response start line (i.e. an object without a `method` attribute), such as httputil.parse_response_start_line('HTTP/1.0 200 OK'); the call completes and returns a boolean instead of raising.
The package data installed by setup.py includes the static test fixture file 'static_foo.txt' alongside the other tornado/test fixture files.

The unsatisfiability (416) determination in StaticFileHandler.get is made using the start offset after negative-start resolution and, in addition to the existing triggers (start not None and start >= size, or end == 0), also treats a range as unsatisfiable when end is not None and start >= end; in every such case the response is status 416 with Content-Type text/plain and Content-Range 'bytes */<size>'.

If the function submitted to IOLoop.run_in_executor raises, the returned Tornado future is completed with that exception (the exception is propagated through the returned future rather than only being stored on the underlying concurrent future).
tenumerate(iterable, start=N) returns an iterator whose yielded index values begin at N (matching builtin enumerate(iterable, start=N)) rather than always beginning at 0.
When total is known and a progress bar is rendered but ncols is falsy (None or 0), format_meter returns the fully formatted meter string 'res' (untrimmed) instead of returning None.

tqdm.format_meter does not raise an exception when called with a falsy (None or 0) total together with a custom numeric unit_scale (unit_scale not in (True, 1)); it returns the stats-only formatted string instead.

An instance constructed with disable=True and no explicit `total` stores `total` as its iterable's length when that is obtainable; e.g. tqdm([0], disable=True).total == 1, tqdm([], disable=True).total == 0, so bool() is True for a non-empty iterable and False for an empty one. When the length cannot be obtained (len(iterable) raises TypeError or AttributeError), the stored total is None.

tqdm.__len__ falls back to the instance's `total` attribute when the iterable has neither a `shape` attribute nor a `__len__` method, and returns `None` (rather than raising AttributeError) for instances where `total` was never set, such as a bar constructed with `disable=True` or one that raised TqdmKeyError for unknown kwargs.

format_sizeof promotes a value to the next SI unit postfix before its fixed-point rendering could display four (or more) digits in the current unit: e.g. format_sizeof(999.99) yields '1.00K' (not '1000'), and format_sizeof(999.99, suffix='B') yields '1.00KB'.
js_to_json matches a single-quoted string that contains a backslash-escaped double quote (\") as one complete string literal, rather than ending the match at that quote.

YoutubeIE._extract_chapters_from_json returns a falsy value (None) without raising when no JSON chapter data can be obtained from the webpage: the webpage is missing/empty, the RELATED_PLAYER_ARGS JSON is absent or unparseable, the parsed player object is not a dict, the watch_next_response entry is absent or not a string, the parsed watch_next_response is not a dict, or the nested chapter list is absent/empty.

Escaped `%%` and `$$` sequences present in the output template are not consumed by the pre-substitution expansion step: `%%` in the template yields a literal single `%` in the returned filename (e.g. outtmpl `%%(height)06d.%(ext)s` returns `%(height)06d.mp4`), and `$$` in the template survives the expansion step unaltered.

Within a quoted operand, the enclosing quote character may be escaped with a backslash (e.g. 'description = "a\"b"'), and the escaped sequence is unescaped in the comparison value (\" becomes " and \' becomes ').

js_to_json leaves double- and single-quoted string literals unchanged by comment handling: a `//` sequence occurring inside a quoted string is not treated as a comment and the string is passed through the existing string-conversion path.

js_to_json recognizes a hexadecimal (0x/0X...) or octal (0 followed by octal digits) numeric literal only when it starts at a word boundary; when the leading '0' is immediately preceded by a word character (letter, digit, or underscore) the sequence is not treated as a number literal and is left unconverted (e.g. js_to_json('10xff') leaves '10xff' rather than producing '1255'), while a literal that does start at a word boundary is still converted to its decimal form as before (e.g. '{0xff:0xff}' still maps to {'255': 255}, and '{077:077}' still maps to {'63': 63}).

When the format-selector function produced by build_format_selector for a direct (single) format token is applied to an empty collection of formats, it yields no formats instead of raising an error (e.g. for 'best'/'worst' it no longer indexes into an empty list).

youtube_dl.utils.strip_jsonp extracts the JSON payload from a JSONP-wrapped string by removing the leading callback wrapper and returns only the captured argument text, including when the JSONP code is followed by a trailing '//' line comment: e.g. for input like 'parseMetadata({...});\n// trailing comment' the returned string is the '{...}' payload with neither the wrapper, the trailing ';' nor the trailing '//' comment.

When ExtractorError is constructed with a truthy cause, the exception's message string includes the cause's repr, appended as ' (caused by <repr(cause)>)' after the message (and after any 'video_id: ' prefix), and this segment appears before the '; please report this issue ...' suffix when that suffix is added.
ArteTVPlus7IE._extract_from_json_url sets the resulting info_dict 'upload_date' from the JSON field 'shootingDate' when that field is present and non-empty, rather than from the 'VDA' field.
limit_length(s, length) returns None when s is None (it does not raise a TypeError).

In a format specification, the right-hand operand of the '+' (merge) operator terminates at an unparenthesized '/' or ',' instead of absorbing it, so '/' and ',' bind looser than '+': e.g. 'bestvideo+bestaudio/best' selects the pick-first between the merged 'bestvideo+bestaudio' pair and 'best', rather than merging bestvideo with the choice (bestaudio/best).

For a mixin column (an object whose info descriptor derives from MixinInfo), reading info.groups yields a read-only ColumnGroups bound to that column (constructed from the column itself); grouping the containing table therefore makes aggregation of the mixin column operate over the table's groups.
