Indexing a Quantity whose unit is a StructuredUnit with a string field key (returning the sub-quantity corresponding to that field) produces a result that does not inherit the source quantity's per-instance `info`; only the field's unit is assigned to the new view.
Calling/set_enabled_constants with any modname other than the supported 'astropyconst13' raises ValueError with a message naming the unsupported modname, before any constant values are changed.

biweight_midvariance of a constant (flattened, axis=None) input array, for which the median absolute deviation is 0, returns 0.0 instead of a NaN/inf result arising from division by zero (so biweight_scale of constant data returns 0.0).

On SQLite, evaluating LPAD, REPEAT, or RPAD with any NULL argument (e.g. a NULL text or NULL length arising from a NULL column) returns NULL rather than raising a user-defined-function error, so text functions using those build NULL results for NULL inputs.

Preparing a value containing an aggregate expression for an INSERT raises FieldError whose message is 'Aggregate functions are not allowed in this query (fieldname=value).' — i.e. it ends with an interpolation of the target field's name and the resolved expression, rather than the bare 'Aggregate functions are not allowed in this query'.

The datetime appended to applied `--list` lines is the applied migration record's `applied` timestamp converted via strftime with the exact format '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S', yielding a wall-clock string like '2021-01-01 12:00:00'.

Running the system checks on a BinaryField that has an explicit default which is a str (e.g. BinaryField(default='') or any other str default) returns a checks.Error with id 'fields.E170' and obj set to that field.

Query.resolve_ref resolves a name present in the annotations via a single lookup and returns that annotation value, so an annotation whose stored value is present is returned and one that resolves against the model fields (not an annotation) continues through the joined-field/join_list rejection path unchanged.

For each unresolvable custom error handler, the emitted urls.E008 Error's message exactly equals "The custom handler{status_code} view '{path}' could not be imported.", where status_code is the numeric handler code (400/403/404/500) and path is the string value stored in the urlconf module's handler{status_code} attribute at the time of the failure.

If accessing the URLconf module (get_resolver().urlconf_module) at reloader startup raises any Exception, the error is swallowed and reloader startup continues: the autoreload_started signal is still sent and the reloader's poll loop still runs instead of the exception propagating.

When add_never_cache_headers is applied to a response whose existing Cache-Control already carries a 'public' directive, the resulting Cache-Control no longer contains 'public' (it is replaced by 'private', per patch_cache_control's mutual-exclusivity between public and private) — i.e. the response's cached-by-shared-caches status is removed.

For a command that declares subcommands via parser.add_subparsers(), when a required argument declared on the selected subcommand's parser (rather than on the top-level parser) is supplied through call_command's **options, call_command forwards that required argument into its argument-parsing simulation and the command executes successfully — it does not raise (e.g. a ValueError from reading option strings, or an argparse error/CommandError about a missing required argument) during option reconstruction.

When settings.DATABASE_ROUTERS is non-empty, the Warning emitted for a duplicate db_table carries hint text "You have configured settings.DATABASE_ROUTERS. Verify that {comma-space-joined colliding model labels} are correctly routed to separate databases.", whereas when routers are not configured the report carries no hint.

make_template_fragment_key no longer URL-encodes vary_on values before hashing: characters that urllib.parse.quote would percent-encode (such as ':', '/', '%', whitespace, or non-ASCII characters) now contribute to the fragment-key MD5 digest in their raw string form, so the returned 'template.cache.<fragment>.<digest>' differs from the old percent-encoded-digest for such inputs.

When the rhs value supplied to an isnull lookup is not a bool instance (True or False), compiling that lookup (IsNull.as_sql) emits a RemovedInDjango40Warning carrying the message 'Using a non-boolean value for an isnull lookup is deprecated, use True or False instead.'; a bool rhs (True or False) does not emit any such warning.

Query.set_group_by() treats an annotation's get_group_by_cols method as accepting the alias argument only if that method's signature declares a parameter named 'alias'. If it does declare such a parameter, get_group_by_cols is called as get_group_by_cols(alias=<annotation alias>); if it does not (including legacy methods that would absorb alias only via **kwargs), a RemovedInDjango40Warning whose text is '`alias=None` must be added to the signature of <module>.<qualname>.get_group_by_cols().' (module and qualname taken from the annotation's class) is emitted and get_group_by_cols() is called with no arguments. In both cases the returned group-by columns are merged into the query's GROUP BY clause.

ModelMultipleChoiceField.__init__() emits a RemovedInDjango40Warning whenever the field's assembled error_messages still contain the deprecated 'list' key (e.g. supplied via the error_messages kwarg), and in that case copies the value of that 'list' override onto the 'invalid_list' key so the override still takes effect.

DatabaseOperations.sql_flush's signature is changed (in base and every backend) from (style, tables, sequences, allow_cascade) to (style, tables, *, reset_sequences=False, allow_cascade=False): the positional sequences argument is removed and sequence-reset behavior is instead requested via the keyword-only reset_sequences boolean (default False). Passing a sequences argument positionally now raises a TypeError.

When the template engine parses a template containing the built-in {% ifequal %}{% endifequal %} tag (invoking the registered ifequal tag function), it emits a Python deprecation warning of category RemovedInDjango40Warning (a PendingDeprecationWarning subclass) with a message stating that the {% ifequal %} template tag is deprecated in favor of {% if %}.

If a FilteredRelation's relation_name itself fails to resolve to a plain chain of relationship fields (i.e. solving it leaves leftover lookup/transform segments), add_filtered_relation raises ValueError with message 'FilteredRelation\'s relation_name cannot contain lookups (got %r).' identifying the offending relation_name.

In MigrationLoader.load_disk, once an app's migrations module is confirmed to be a regular (non-namespace) package (it has both a __file__ and a __path__), the app's label is added to migrated_apps unconditionally — the previously conditional logic that would instead add it to unmigrated_apps when the package contained no migration submodules and ignore_no_migrations was False is removed, so an app with a real but empty migrations package is now treated as migrated regardless of the number of migration submodules it contains and regardless of the ignore_no_migrations value.

A combined arithmetic expression (CombinedExpression using ADD, SUB, MUL or DIV) whose two source sub-expressions have output fields that are integer-kind fields — i.e. any pair that are each IntegerField or an IntegerField subclass such as AutoField, SmallAutoField or BigAutoField (distinct classes, e.g. a plain IntegerField from Value(3) combined with an AutoField column) — resolves to an IntegerField output instead of raising a 'mixed output-field types' FieldError.

When rendering a blocktranslate/blocktrans tag that carries a plural count (i.e. a `count` option that provides both a counter variable and counter expression), if the value that the counter expression resolves to in the render context is not one of the numeric types Decimal, float, or int (e.g. it is a str, list, None, or other non-numeric type), render() raises a TemplateSyntaxError rather than proceeding to plural-form selection and '%'-formatting. The raised error's message is "%r argument to %r tag must be a number." where the first %r is the counter variable name and the second is the tag name (blocktranslate/blocktrans).

When deletion via Collector.collect is blocked by protected foreign keys and it aggregates references into a ProtectedError, the raised exception's `protected_objects` attribute (and the second positional element of its `args` tuple, which is what its repr renders) is a materialized `set` of the referencing objects — never a lazy iterator such as an `itertools.chain` — so the attribute is directly inspectable/iterable and each distinct referencing object appears once.

The durability nesting check of Atomic is subject to the class-level private flag Atomic._ensure_durability (True by default) such that when a subclass (or instance class) sets _ensure_durability to False, entering a durable=True atomic block nested inside another atomic block no longer raises RuntimeError.

ModelAdmin now defines the public method get_formset_kwargs(self, request, obj, inline, prefix), exposing a subclass-overridable point for computing the keyword arguments with which each inline formset is instantiated.

Constructing django.core.cache.backends.memcached.MemcachedCache (calling MemcachedCache(server, params)) emits a RemovedInDjango41Warning whose message states that MemcachedCache is deprecated in favor of PyMemcacheCache and PyLibMCCache.

BaseForm.get_initial_for_field returns the resolved initial value (the value from self.initial with the field's initial as fallback, or the result of calling a callable value) with its microsecond attribute zeroed (replace(microsecond=0)) whenever that value is an instance of datetime.datetime or datetime.time AND field.widget.supports_microseconds is False.

While generating an AddField operation for an added field, if the (default-adjusted) field being added is unique, has a default that is not models.NOT_PROVIDED, and has a callable default, MigrationAutodetector calls questioner.ask_unique_callable_default_addition(field_name, model_name) for that field; when any of those three conditions is false the hook is not invoked for that field.

The squashmigrations management command refuses to run when the on-disk destination migration file it would write already exists: instead of creating/overwriting any file at that path, it fails the command by raising CommandError whose message contains the phrase 'already exists' and the new migration name.
MultiWidget.id_for_label(id_) returns the empty string '' for every argument, so that a field-level <label> associated with a MultiWidget never points (via for=) to its first subwidget's HTML id.

When QuerySet.bulk_update is called updating a relation field, and some object in `objs` has that relation cached to an unsaved related object (pk is None), bulk_update raises ValueError with message 'bulk_update() prohibited to prevent data loss due to unsaved related object '<field>'.' instead of silently persisting a null/stale key for that field.

For a ResolverMatch whose func is the callable produced by a class-based view's View.as_view() (i.e. func has a `view_class` attribute, with the wrapper's `__name__` left as 'view'), ResolverMatch stores `_func_path` as the wrapped view class's fully-qualified dotted path `view_class.__module__ + '.' + view_class.__name__` (e.g. `app.views.LazyRedirectView`) instead of the wrapper callable's own path `func.__module__ + '.' + func.__name__` (which would be `app.views.view`). As a consequence, `ResolverMatch.__repr__` prints `func=<module>.<ClassName>` for such class-based views, and when the matched pattern has no url_name its `view_name` components the same class path.

When BaseHandler.adapt_method_mode adapts a synchronous method for an async mode (is_async=True and method_is_async=False) with debug=True, it emits a DEBUG record on the 'django.request' logger whose formatted message is 'Synchronous handler adapted for {name}.'.

Calling CryptPasswordHasher's constructor (instantiating the class) emits a RemovedInDjango50Warning with message 'django.contrib.auth.hashers.CryptPasswordHasher is deprecated.' before normal base-class initialization proceeds.

BaseFormSet.empty_form returns a form instance (rather than raising a TypeError about receiving multiple values for the same keyword argument) when the formset was constructed with form_kwargs whose keys overlap the reserved empty-form keyword arguments empty_permitted, auto_id, prefix, use_required_attribute, and/or renderer.

When bind_template raises the informative TypeError described above (after a context processor's result caused a TypeError during merging), the newly raised TypeError carries the original TypeError as its chained cause (__cause__), so both exceptions remain visible to the caller.

When a StepValueValidator is constructed with a non-None offset and the value fails the step check, the raised ValidationError conveys code "step_size" with the offset-aware message text ("starting from %(offset)s, e.g. %(offset)s, %(valid_value1)s, %(valid_value2)s, and so on.") and params limit_value, offset, valid_value1 (= offset + limit_value), and valid_value2 (= offset + 2*limit_value).

matplotlib.pyplot.switch_backend, when called with a requested backend whose (exact string) name differs from the currently set rcParams['backend'] value, closes all open figures (destroys/removes all figure managers via close('all')) after switching to the new backend.

A legend created with a string loc whose first space-separated token is 'outside' (e.g. 'outside upper left', 'outside upper center', 'outside upper right', 'outside lower center', 'outside lower right', 'outside lower left', 'outside right upper', 'outside right lower', 'outside left upper', 'outside left lower') is accepted: the 'outside' token is consumed and the remainder is mapped onto an otherwise valid standard loc value, so construction succeeds rather than failing as an unrecognized loc. The token order matters ('outside right upper' maps to a different resolved location than 'outside upper right').

During automatic legend handle collection, a candidate artist (including a .Text) whose label is neither empty nor '_nolegend_' but for which no legend handler can be found in the effective handler map is no longer silently discarded; it triggers an external warning of the form "Legend does not support handles for {ConcreteTypeName} instances." pointing to the legend_guide 'implementing-a-custom-legend-handler' section, and that artist is NOT emitted as a legend handle.

Calling selector.set_handle_props(**handle_props) applies the given properties to each of the selector's handle/vertex artists (e.g. RectangleSelector corner/edge/center markers, SpanSelector edge handles, PolygonSelector vertex handles), so their rendered appearance is updated immediately; the props are also recorded in _handle_props for future handles.

copy.copy of a TaggedValue returns a new TaggedValue holding the same value and unit as the original (shallow copy, sharing the underlying value object), rather than falling back to deep/reduce-based copying.

In PS/EPS output, when a clip-path that has not been seen before is drawn, RendererPS defines a bound PostScript procedure whose name is 'c' followed by the clip path's zero-based sequence number formatted in decimal (so the clip procedures defined/used in the emitted .ps/.eps file are c0, c1, ..., c10, ... rather than c0,c1,...,ca,cb,... for counts >= 10), and that decimal name (not a hexadecimal rendering) is the value cached in _clip_paths and re-referenced whenever the same clip path recurs.

matplotlib.style.use (and the style.context context manager, which delegates to use) accepts, as a style specification, a string of the dotted form "package.style_name" where "package" is an importable Python package; the rcParams defined in the file located inside that package at <package>/style_name.mplstyle are read and applied (only the parameters actually listed in that file). Dotted names spanning subpackages (e.g. "dotted.package.name" resolving within dotted/package/) are likewise supported.

Calling Axis.set_ticks with labels=None (labels not provided) while passing additional keyword arguments raises ValueError with the message 'labels argument cannot be None when kwargs are passed', rather than silently ignoring those kwargs.

If eventplot is given an array-like alpha whose length (other than a broadcastable single-element value) differs from the number of position sets, eventplot raises ValueError with message 'alpha and positions are unequal sized sequences'.

imsave raises a ValueError (with a message indicating the format does not support metadata) instead of silently ignoring *metadata* when saving to any raster format handled by Pillow other than 'png' (e.g. jpeg, tiff, webp); metadata continues to be honoured for 'png' and for the vector formats 'pdf'/'ps'/'eps'/'svg', and a None metadata still passes through unchanged.

Calling Figure.tight_layout() must not cause the figure to be re-armed with a working automatic tight-layout engine through the rc parameter figure.autolayout: in particular, when rcParams['figure.autolayout'] is True, after fig.tight_layout() returns the figure does not hold a freshly-installed TightLayoutEngine, so subsequent draws do not keep re-running tight layout as a side effect of the tight_layout() cleanup.

When a shared sibling Axes's limit is updated as part of propagating an emitted limit change, that update is applied non-recursively (the sibling _set_lim is invoked with emit=False) and the sibling's own '{name}lim_changed' event is then fired at most once per originating change, so the event does not cascade or get re-emitted again through the shared-axis group.

Axes3D.plot builds its data line through _get_lines._plot_args passing the invoking 3D Axes itself, so unit processing/axis update from plotted (unit-bearing, e.g. y) data applies to the 3D axes the plot was called on even when that axes' _get_lines handler originated elsewhere.

For a mathtext ('$...$') marker, the marker's centering translation and size-normalization scale are derived from the curve-aware geometric bounding box of the mathtext text path obtained via Path.get_extents() (which returns the actual extent swept by the glyph outline Bézier segments, evaluated including curve extrema) rather than from the axis-aligned min/max span of the text path's raw vertices/control points.

Calling Axis.set_ticks(ticks) (with labels=None and minor not given) while passing one or more extra keyword-only styling/Text arguments (i.e. kwargs is non-empty) raises a ValueError whose message states 'Incorrect use of keyword argument' followed by the repr of the first such keyword argument passed, and goes on to say that keyword arguments other than 'minor' modify the text labels and can only be used if 'labels' are passed as well.

For a vector that is not entirely missing, variable_type determines the reported type from only the present (non-null) entries: it first returns 'numeric' only when every entry is missing; otherwise it removes all missing entries and then applies boolean detection and numeric/datetime/categorical inference to the remaining values. Concretely, an object/extension column that (ignoring nulls) is made up solely of numeric values is reported as 'numeric' rather than categorical, and one made up solely of datetime values as 'datetime', regardless of the presence/position of missing entries.

Mounting a prefix with Session.mount replaces the previously registered adapter for that exact prefix if one exists, updates that adapter's value in place, and still keeps every mounted adapter (including that remounted prefix) reachable for dispatch, so the registry always contains one entry per distinct prefix with the latest-mounted adapter winning for that prefix.
merge_hooks(request_hooks, session_hooks) returns request_hooks unchanged as the merged result whenever session_hooks is None or session_hooks has an empty list ('[]') for the 'response' event.

PreparedRequest.copy() produces a new PreparedRequest whose `_cookies` CookieJar is an independent copy of the source request's jar, so a copied request still carries (and an independent copy of) the cookies of the original.

HTTPAdapter.send no longer eagerly reads the response body (`.content`) for a non-stream request (stream=False); it builds and returns the Response without having preloaded/decode-read the content, so a Content-Encoding or chunked decoding failure of the raw response is not raised by send itself (the response body is left for the caller/another layer to consume).
PreparedRequest.prepare_method raises ValueError('Request method cannot be "None"') when given a method of None, rather than silently storing self.method as None.

When evaluating Request.full_url (directly, or transitively via Request.send/path_url/response building), if the parsed netloc causes netloc.encode('idna') to raise a UnicodeError (e.g. an empty, too-long, or otherwise invalid IDNA label in an otherwise scheme-supported URL), the operation raises an InvalidURL exception carrying the message 'URL has an invalid label.' rather than letting the raw UnicodeError propagate out.

DataArray and Dataset (both subclassing common.DataWithCoords) each expose a `weighted(weights)` method that returns a weighted-operations accessor object constructed from the object under reduction and the provided weights (`DataArrayWeighted` for DataArray, `DatasetWeighted` for Dataset).

ZarrBackendEntrypoint now provides a guess_can_open that returns True only when filename_or_obj is a string whose extension from os.path.splitext is exactly '.zarr'; if os.path.splitext(filename_or_obj) raises TypeError (e.g. non-string input), it returns False. Previously zarr had no guess_can_open override.

xr.polyval returns an output whose non-degree broadcast dimension ordering is anchored on the evaluation coordinate `coord`: the Horner accumulator is seeded from a full broadcast (all-zero DataArray) matching `coord`'s dimensions/coordinates, placed as the leading operand of the first addition with the highest-degree coefficient term `coeffs.isel(degree_dim=max_deg, drop=True)`, so that when the leading-coefficient term and `coord` disagree in dimension order the returned array's dimension ordering/index structure and (DataArray) name follow `coord` rather than the coefficient array.

duck_array_ops.is_duck_array (utils-level utility is_duck_array): an object that has ndim, shape and dtype attributes and implements __array_namespace__ counts as a duck array even when it does NOT provide both __array_function__ and __array_ufunc__; previously such an object was NOT a duck array.

For each variable of the dataset, _protect_dataset_variables_inplace replaces the stored data with a CopyOnWriteArray wrapping of variable._data (itself wrapped in a MemoryCachedArray whenever the cache argument is truthy) exactly for those variables whose name is NOT a member of dataset._indexes; variables whose name IS one of the dataset's active indexes are skipped and left unmodified (their .data is never re-assigned).

Calling enable/disable/disable_next on a PyLinter with a *numeric* message id (accompanied by a resolvable symbol and a non-empty module/current_name) appends a ManagedMessage(name, msgid, symbol, line, is_disabled) record to that PyLinter's own instance attribute `_by_id_managed_msgs` (initialized in __init__). The by-id managed-message state is now per-linter-instance rather than residing in a class-level list shared by MessagesHandlerMixIn, so two distinct PyLinter objects keep independent such records.
pylint.constants defines DeletedMessage as a NamedTuple whose fields are 'msgid' (str), 'symbol' (str), and 'old_names' (a list of (str,str) pairs defaulting to the empty list).

Constructing a checker (an instance of BaseChecker or any of its subclasses such as BaseTokenChecker/BaseRawFileChecker) whose class sets a truthy `__implements__` attribute causes a DeprecationWarning to be raised with a message stating that using the __implements__ inheritance pattern for BaseChecker is no longer supported and that child classes should only inherit BaseChecker or the other checker types from pylint.checkers.

Invoking the pylint Run entry point with no file/package arguments (and with --version / pylint-config command handling not otherwise short-circuiting) prints the single line "No files to lint: exiting." to stdout and exits with code 32, instead of printing the full linter help text.
pylint.interfaces exports a CONFIDENCE_MAP dict that maps each confidence level name from CONFIDENCE_LEVEL_NAMES to its corresponding Confidence entry in CONFIDENCE_LEVELS.

on_rm_rf_error now accepts the calling convention used by shutil.rmtree(onexc=...), where its exception argument ('exc') is a bare BaseException instance, in addition to the legacy (type, exception, traceback) exc-info triple; under the bare-instance convention it discriminates errors with outcomes matching those for the triple form: a FileNotFoundError causes it to return False without warning, any other non-PermissionError exception causes it to emit a PytestWarning and return False, and a PermissionError reaching the deletion handling (chmod-and-retry vs. 'unknown function' warning) behaves as before.

The new DatetimeFormatter formatter's formatTime(record, datefmt): when datefmt is non-empty and contains the '%f' directive, it returns the record's time rendered by datetime.strftime (which understands %f), substituting %f with a 6-digit microsecond field derived from the record's msecs attribute (its milliseconds converted to microseconds) within the record's local time & zone; when datefmt is empty or contains no '%f', formatTime(record, datefmt) returns exactly what the standard logging.Formatter.formatTime would return, so date formats without %f produce unchanged output.

_pytest.deprecated defines JUNIT_XML_DEFAULT_FAMILY as a PytestDeprecationWarning whose message is "The 'junit_family' default value will change to 'xunit2' in pytest 6.0.\nAdd 'junit_family=legacy' to your pytest.ini file to silence this warning and make your suite compatible."

_pytest.pytester_assertions.assert_outcomes: its `warnings` parameter is optional (default None); when it is None the assertion imposes no constraint on the actual warnings outcome count, and only when warned-parsed count is supplied explicitly (non-None) is the actual warnings count (parsed from the outcomes dict, defaulting to 0 if absent/not listed) required to equal it (mismatch makes the assertion fail).

The lazily re-derived `obj` value of a TestCaseFunction is the test method attribute obtained from the test class itself (i.e. an unbound method), in contrast to a bound method attached to a test-class instance; in particular the lazy lookup does not depend on, and does not need, the setUp-created TestCase instance (`_testcase`/bound `_obj`), so it still succeeds after `teardown()` has cleared those.

In check_methods_subset_invariance, comparing a method's whole-set result with its per-sample results handles tuple-valued method outputs (e.g. some score_samples forms): only the first element of the returned tuple is used in the comparison, for both the whole-set call and each single-sample call.

Calling LabelEncoder.inverse_transform with an empty (0-sample) input on a fitted encoder returns an empty numpy array (np.array([])) rather than proceeding through the unseen-label validation and array indexing.
FunctionTransformer's __init__ validate parameter defaults to None rather than True: an instance created without passing an explicit validate value has its validate attribute set to None.

fit(X, y=None) remains available and continues to return self, and its observable fitting behavior is unchanged even though the implementation now performs the estimation by delegating to fit_predict(X, y) internally.

In check_array, an input object that exposes both a `dtypes` attribute and an `__array__` attribute but whose `.dtypes` is empty or has no length (e.g. a pandas Series holding a single scalar dtype) is accepted and validated through all the normal conversion/validation/warning steps without crashing on a 0-d iteration; in particular it no longer records `dtypes_orig` from that `.dtypes` attribute, so it does not enter the end-of-function multiple-original-dtypes DataConversionWarning comparison path regardless of `warn_on_dtype` and any resulting dtype difference from the converted array.

When GridSearchCV/RandomizedSearchCV.fit schedules fits over the product of the candidate params and the CV split iterator but zero individual fits are actually produced (e.g. the CV iterator yields no splits, or there are no candidates), fit raises a ValueError whose message reports that no fits were performed rather than proceeding to accumulate/format an empty result set.

When explicit categories are provided at fit, for each column whose own dtype is numerical (not object) the provided categories for that column, cast to that column's dtype, must be sorted — if they are not, fit raises ValueError('Unsorted categories are not supported for numerical categories'); object-dtype columns are exempt from this requirement regardless of the dtype of other columns in the same input.

When fit on training data where the requested n_quantiles exceeds the number of samples (n_samples), QuantileTransformer.fit issues a UserWarning reporting that n_quantiles is greater than the total number of samples and that n_quantiles is set to n_samples.

When VarianceThreshold.fit is called with the default threshold of 0.0 on sparse (CSR/CSC) input, any feature column whose samples are numerically constant across all rows is given an effective variance of 0 (self.variances_ = min(mean_variance_axis result, min_max_axis-derived range) = 0), so that the feature is dropped rather than being kept due to a floating-point residual variance.

_euclidean_distances_upcast accepts an optional batch_size argument (in addition to X, XX, Y, YY). When batch_size is None, its chunk size is auto-derived from the X/Y sparsity-based memory heuristic as before; when a batch_size value is supplied, that value is taken directly as the chunk size for batching over both X rows and Y rows (skipping the auto memory-based computation) and the remaining per-X-chunk Y-batch iteration proceeds using that chunk size.

Calling MLPClassifier.partial_fit or MLPRegressor.partial_fit (stochastic solver 'adam'/'sgd') on an estimator whose early_stopping parameter is True raises a ValueError with message "partial_fit does not support early_stopping=True", rather than continuing training. This applies regardless of whether the model was previously fit with early_stopping (which would leave best_loss_ = None) or is a first partial_fit call, and it occurs before validation-set splitting / weight initialization of the incremental pass.

Both MLPClassifier and MLPRegressor accept a new `max_fun` constructor keyword argument (with default 15000) which is stored as the public instance attribute/estimator parameter `self.max_fun` and forwarded to the shared BaseMultilayerPerceptron initializer; it is visible through the estimator's parameter interface (get_params).

At import time of sphinx.addnodes, SIG_ELEMENTS contains exactly the standard signature leaf node classes desc_sig_space, desc_sig_name, desc_sig_operator, desc_sig_punctuation, desc_sig_keyword, desc_sig_keyword_type, desc_sig_literal_number, desc_sig_literal_string and desc_sig_literal_char, each of which is declared as a desc_sig_element subclass with _sig_element=True.

When partitioning a docstring line into a leading part and its colon-separated description, a text run starting with the literal token ``:meta `` followed by further colon-delimited content (of shape `:meta KEY: VALUE...`, i.e. a ``:meta ...: ...`` construct) is treated as a single atomic/protected unit, so none of the colons inside it is taken as the leading/description boundary; text such as a ``:meta``-style embedded annotation on a parsed line is not split in the middle and remains attributed to the preceding field rather than being shifted into the description.

autodoc exposes a new public class `ObjectMember`; constructing `ObjectMember(name, obj, skipped=False)` yields an instance that behaves/comparatively equals the 2-tuple `(name, obj)` and additionally exposes attributes `__name__` (== name), `object` (== obj), and `skipped` (default False, settable to True).

A new Sphinx configuration value `autodoc_typehints_description_target` is registered with a default value of `'all'`, restricted to the two allowed values `'all'` and `'documented'` (Sphinx's enum validator rejects any other value), and flagged as an upgrade/rebuild-triggering setting.

Autosummary's internal documenter works with classes without error even though its synthetic app/config is built outside normal application setup, because the synthetic config used there also declares `autodoc_class_signature` with the same default value ('mixed').

When the linkcheck extension is set up (module setup()), the 'linkcheck-process-uri' event no longer registers rewrite_github_anchor as a handler, so github.com hrefs/fragments are no longer rewritten to prefix their fragment with 'user-content-' during hyperlink collection/checking; a github.com URL such as '.../sphinx#documentation' is collected and checked under its original fragment rather than being rewritten to '.../sphinx#user-content-documentation'.

LatexPrinter._print_SingularityFunction emits the SingularityFunction with its exponent rendered as a braced superscript group `^{<power>}` directly after the closing `>` of the angle-bracket expression, with no space between caret and exponent, so that exponent values that contain a leading minus sign or are multi-character (e.g. -1, -2) produce valid output rather than being split off by whitespace from the caret (e.g. latex(SingularityFunction(x, 0, -1)) equals r'{\langle x \rangle}^{-1}', not r'{\langle x \rangle}^ -1').

Matrix.is_upper_hessenberg evaluates to True for a rectangular matrix having more rows than columns whose entries that lie in the strictly-below-subdiagonal band within the matrix's actual columns are all zero — in particular an all-zero k×m matrix with k > m reports is_upper_hessenberg == True rather than raising an IndexError from iterating a column index ≥ cols.

When the first argument is a Poly with exactly one generator and k is a positive Integer (with x finite and not +/-oo), RisingFactorial.eval returns the expanded functional product of the shifted polynomial, i.e. x(y)*x(y+1)*...*x(y+k-1) as a Poly (e.g. rf(Poly(x**3, x), 2) -> Poly(x**6 + 3*x**5 + 3*x**4 + x**3, x, domain='ZZ')).

Calling the module-level sympy.polys.polytools.degree on a non-Poly, non-numeric Expr that has more than one distinct free symbol raises type-errors.TypeError when no explicit symbolic generator is supplied (i.e. when the gen argument is numeric, including its default value 0), instead of returning the degree with respect to the canonically-chosen first generator.
Modulo (Mod or %) with a divisor that is exactly zero raises ZeroDivisionError rather than attempting to evaluate the remainder.

exptrigsimp no longer accepts a 'simplify' keyword argument; its signature is now exptrigsimp(expr), so a call passing a simplify= flag is a TypeError, and the transformation set it applies to its input is no longer conditional on such a flag (the one library caller, top-level simplify(), which formerly disabled this, now invokes the full transformation).

Mod.eval reduces Mod(p, q) when the dividend p is a Mul containing at least one inner Mod factor whose divisor equals the outer divisor q: it folds the remaining non-Mod factors of p into the Mod, returning a product equal to Mod(net, q) where net is the product of the non-Mod factors multiplied with the product of the dividend arguments (args[0]) of all of p's inner Mod factors. E.g. Mod(a*Mod(b,q), q) reduces to Mod(a*b, q) (non-mod factor a moved onto inner dividend b), given the inner divisor matches q.

When JuliaCodePrinter prints a Mul whose factors include a Pow with exponent exactly -1 whose base is itself a Mul holding more than one factor, the Julia division denominator text for that base (which uses elementwise './' 'as appropriate') is wrapped in parentheses so that the denominator product is grouped rather than left as a bare product after the division operator.

CodePrinter._print_Function treats an applied Function whose name is not among the printer's known_functions and which has no inlined `_imp_` Lambda conditionally: when it satisfies expr.is_Function and the printer's `allow_unknown_functions` setting is truthy, it is emitted as a literal call of the form `<printed func>(<printed arg1>, <printed arg2>, …)` (the function name and each argument printed recursively, comma-joined with ', ') instead of being routed to _print_not_supported; when `allow_unknown_functions` is False (or expr.is_Function is false) such a Function is still recorded as Not supported and returned via the pre-existing fallback.

In periodicity(f, symbol), when f is a Mod whose argument a is neither symbol itself nor a TrigonometricFunction, the linear-period shortcut returning Abs(n/a.diff(symbol)) is used only when a is a polynomial in symbol (and degree(a, symbol)==1 and symbol is not in the free symbols of the Mod modulus n); for a Mod argument a that is not a polynomial in symbol, this shortcut is no longer taken.
srepr(S.Integers) (ReprPrinter._print_Integers) returns the string 'Integers' rather than the emptyPrinter fallback 'Integers()'.
For a power with a base known to be zero and an exponent known to be real, Pow.is_negative always returns False (a zero base to any real exponent is never negative).
A sign expression whose argument is known to be zero under the assumptions refines to 0 (IntegerZero / S.Zero).

Expr equality (__eq__) against a Python native string returns False regardless of the string text (e.g. Symbol('x') == 'x' is False and Integer(1) == '1' is False), rather than sympify-parsing the string content and comparing against it (which could otherwise make Symbol('x') == 'x' evaluate to True).
S.Rationals.boundary equals S.Reals (the whole real line), rather than Rationals itself.

For such an integer-ImageSet vs. Integers/imageSet intersection, when f(n)=g(m) admits exactly one parametric (infinite) solution family for n with a single free symbol, the intersection is returned as the ImageSet { f(h(t)) : t in Integers } with the resulting lambda expression expanded.

When a MatMul consists of two factors, one being a MatAdd matrix expression and the other a Rational scalar, canonicalization (MatMul.doit/canonicalize) now distributes the scalar over the MatAdd rather than leaving the scalar-times-sum as an unevaluated product. That is, the product of the Rational `r` with the MatAdd of terms, written in either factor order (scalar before the sum or after the sum), evaluates to a MatAdd of the scalar applied to each term individually; e.g. `r*(A+B)` (and the reversed-order form) evaluates to `r*A + r*B`, each `r*term` result itself being passed through doit.

Constructing a symbolic Range collapses it to the canonical empty range (start=stop=0, step=1, i.e. Range(0)) whenever the computed member count (stop-start)/step is exactly 0 (start and stop symbolically equal) or is negative (a symbolically-descending or vacuous span), rather than merely detecting the trivial start==stop case.

Each value in the relations dict passed to the CoordSystem constructor must, per stored (source-system-name, target-system-name) key, carry both the source system's coordinate symbols and the target's transformed-coordinate expressions: canonicalization stores an entry as the 2-tuple (tuple-of-source-symbols, tuple-of-target-expressions). A Lambda value is converted using its signature and expr; any other value has element [0] taken as the source-symbols tuple and element [1] as the target-expressions tuple.

pow_rep_recursive, when asked to select exactly one more term (k == 1) to complete the remaining amount n_remaining, resolves that final term directly instead of recursing further: it emits the tuple terms + (r,) where r is the exact p-th integer root of n_remaining, and emits that tuple only if n_remaining is an exact p-th power (r^p == n_remaining) and r <= n_i; if n_remaining is not an exact p-th power or its exact root exceeds n_i it yields nothing, and in every k == 1 case the generator returns immediately rather than descending more recursion frames for that term.
In the cgs_gauss unit system, the scale factor of ampere is set to 10*speed_of_light*statcoulomb/second.

The ITRS frame carries an EarthLocation 'location' frame attribute whose default is the centre of the Earth, so an ITRS frame/coordinate can be created (or defaulted) with either an explicit topocentric (non-geocentric) observing site or, by default, the geocenter, and it can be transformed to a topocentric ITRS that is offset from the geocenter.

CDS-format division of units is now left-associative: a CDS unit string containing two or more consecutive unparenthesised '/' separators groups them left to right, so that terms of the form U/V/W are parsed as (U/V)/W — physically U·V⁻¹·W⁻¹, with each unit after the first '/' ending up in the denominator — rather than the previous right-expansion U/(V/W). For example parsing 'J/m/s/kpc2' (or 'erg/cm2/s', etc.) with format='cds' yields the composite whose power vector assigns power −1 to m, s and kpc2, i.e. the base equivalent of J/(m·s·kpc2), instead of the old J/(m/(s/kpc2)) nesting.

When Quantity is constructed from an existing Quantity input (no unit change) with dtype=None and copy=True, an integer-kind input Quantity is promoted to float64, whereas a float16 (or other float-kind) input Quantity keeps its original float dtype instead of being widened to float64 — only integer-kind inputs trigger the float default in this code path.

DatabaseClient.runshell_db launches psql via subprocess.run with check=True, so a non-zero exit status of psql propagates as a CalledProcessError (i.e. the call does not silently swallow psql failures).

parse_duration, when matching the standard 'HH:MM:SS[.ffffff]' format, accepts an optional single leading '-' sign placed immediately before the time portion (before the hours term, or before the first term when there is no hours term), and that sign, when present, negates the entire time portion as a whole rather than only its leading (hours) term — e.g. "-01:02:03" yields a timedelta equal to negative (1 hour, 2 minutes, 3 seconds).

HttpResponseBase.make_bytes, given a memoryview argument, returns the underlying raw bytes of the memoryview (equivalent to bytes(value)) instead of encoding the memoryview's str() representation in self.charset.

django.utils.html.escape(text) returns a SafeString whose content is the input str(text) with HTML-significant characters encoded, namely: & becomes &, < becomes <, > becomes >, " becomes ", and ' becomes '.

Field.get_choices returns a relation's related objects in the related model's default ordering (the ordering of its default manager, i.e. its Meta.ordering) when the 'ordering' argument is empty/() — instead of stripping that default ordering by appending a blank order_by() — and orders them by the supplied non-empty 'ordering' fields when such are given.

URL resolution through regex-based patterns (re_path/url, via RegexPattern.match) excludes from the resolved kwargs any named capture group whose value is None (i.e., an optional named group in the regex that did not participate in the match). Such an unmatched optional group no longer appears as a keyword argument with value None; it is dropped from the match's kwargs entirely.

When resolve_lookup_value is given a list/tuple whose elements are themselves lists/tuples, the nested iterables are resolved recursively and each nested level likewise preserves its own container type (list stays list, tuple stays tuple) across all nesting depths, rather than only the outermost level being handled.

SQLDeleteCompiler.single_alias returns True for a delete whose query references only its model's base table (exactly one alias has a nonzero refcount once the base table is ensured present), even when the base-table alias's stored alias_refcount would otherwise be zero because all query-time references had been released; only when additional join aliases are also active does single_alias evaluate to False.

DecimalField.to_python, when the non-None, non-float value it is converting via decimal.Decimal(value) causes a TypeError or ValueError (in addition to the already-handled decimal.InvalidOperation) — e.g. a dict, list, or other unsupported input — raises a django.core.exceptions.ValidationError with the field's 'invalid' error message, code='invalid', and the offending value in params, rather than letting the raw TypeError/ValueError propagate.

On a backend with has_native_duration_field False, when both operands of a CombinedExpression resolve to internal type DurationField the expression is not wrapped through DurationExpression/combine_duration_expression; it is compiled by the ordinary branch that compiles each operand and joins them with connection.ops.combine_expression and the raw connector, so it is applied exactly once.

During CombinedExpression.resolve_expression, a combined arithmetic expression whose two operands resolve to different field internal types where at least one is DurationField (a DurationField mixed with a non-duration field) is rewritten, at resolution time, into a DurationExpression and recursively resolved; the rewritten DurationExpression is resolved as a duration-arithmetic expression on every backend rather than only on backends lacking a native duration field.

HttpResponseBase.delete_cookie forces Secure on the deletion cookie (in addition to the pre-existing __Secure-/__Host- name-prefix logic) when the given samesite value is 'none' (case-insensitive), so that a cookie previously set with SameSite=None can actually be deleted by a browser.

When FileExtensionValidator rejects an upload whose extension is not allowed, the ValidationError it raises carries the rejected file value in params under 'value', in addition to its existing 'extension' and 'allowed_extensions' keys.

For every URL kwarg captured by a TemplateView, the value that _wrap_url_kwargs_with_deprecation_warning places into its returned mapping retains the deprecation contract: evaluating it as its underlying value triggers a RemovedInDjango40Warning whose message says TemplateView passing URL kwargs to the context is deprecated and instructs referencing the key through view.kwargs in the template, and yields the originally captured value.

Frame generation for each contributing exception skips traceback frames whose frame locals set __traceback_hide__ to a truthy value, and otherwise reports every frame of that exception's traceback in tb_next order; the last reported frame of the whole list corresponds to the last non-hidden frame reached.

When a lazy proxy value appears on the LEFT-hand side of the addition operator (evaluated as ``<lazy_proxy> + <other>``), the lazy proxy is forced to its concrete value and the operation's result is ``<cast concrete value> + <other>`` (delegating to the concrete value's ``__add__``) rather than raising a TypeError.

ThreadedWSGIServer's __init__ accepts an optional keyword argument connections_override (defaulting to None) and stores the passed value unchanged on the instance as the attribute connections_override.

BaseDatabaseOperations.year_lookup_bounds_for_date_field gains an optional iso_year keyword flag; when iso_year=True the returned [lower, upper] pair spans the ISO-8601 week-numbering year equal to value, not the calendar year value — the lower bound is the day on which ISO week 1 of value begins, and the upper bound is the last day of that ISO week-numbering year (the day before ISO week 1 of value+1 begins), each still passed through the same date-value adaptation used by the calendar path.

The `to_field` keyword is added only to relations classified as ForeignKey; when a relation column is classified as OneToOneField (unique or primary-key), no `to_field` keyword argument is added to the generated output even if the referenced column is not the referenced table's primary key.

get_language_from_path() recognizes a path whose initial language-prefix segment is a code of the form word('-word|@word){0,2} — i.e. comprised of up to three subtags joined by single '-' or '@' (e.g. en-latn-us, zh-hant-tw) — extracting that whole three-subtag code as the candidate language code; for a path prefix representing a supported language (present in LANGUAGES and with a matching locale file), it returns the corresponding supported language variant instead of None. (Previously only one- and two-subtag prefixes such as en, en-us, pt-br could be parsed; a three-subtag prefix such as en-latn-us caused the code not to be extracted.)

When RenameIndex.database_forwards resolves the pre-renaming (from-state / actually-present) index and that index's name already equals self.new_name — i.e. the operation is a no-op because nothing would change — it performs no database schema change (does not call schema_editor.rename_index, and does not require the to_state index lookup) and returns normally, rather than attempting to rename an index to a name it already carries (which previously triggered a duplicate-relation error on re-application of an unnamed-index rename after its no-op backward step).

On any path where floatformat cannot produce a formatted result and echoes the input value back unmodified (i.e. when arg is not a valid integer magnitude, or when the value cannot be processed as a Decimal), a Decimal input is echoed as its plain digit string (str form), e.g. '555.555', rather than as its repr Python-literal form "Decimal('555.555')".

When ServerHandler processes a HEAD request and the WSGI application's response set a Content-Length header, that Content-Length header is removed before the response is finalized, so the HEAD response does not advertise a body length derived from the (stripped) payload.

AbstractBaseUser.get_session_auth_fallback_hash() is a generator that, for each entry of settings.SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS in order, yields a fallback session-auth-hash computed from the user's password field using that fallback secret as the HMAC secret (i.e., it yields len(settings.SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS) values, each a distinct fallback-secret-derived hash).

When FileResponse serves a compressed file whose basename ends in '.br' and no explicit content_type is provided, the response's Content-Type header is set to 'application/x-brotli' (rather than the guessed type such as text/*).

Elements of the input sequence that are already marked safe (SafeString/SafeData instances or objects exposing an HTML representation via `__html__`) are included in the returned list unchanged with no double-escaping applied.

When serializing in pk format (serializer invoked without natural keys) an object that has an auto-created many-to-many field whose target model's default manager carries a select_related on its queryset, the XML serializer (django.core.serializers.xml_serializer.Serializer) succeeds in iterating the m2m relations and emits one <object pk=...> reference per related object, rather than raising the 'Field ... cannot be both deferred and traversed using select_related at the same time' error.

For a method bound to a class nested inside an enclosing class/namespace, the serialized output must include the complete nesting path (all enclosing dotted segments) so the emitted expression names the actual class, and the 'import <module>' for that class's module is still emitted.

Calling Axes.set_xlim with a reversed (descending) request on a log-scaled x-axis — e.g. ax.set_xlim(x_max, x_min) where the first argument > the second — produces an inverted (descending) x view interval instead of being silently re-sorted ascending by log-scale limit adjustment: afterwards get_xlim()/viewLim.intervalx returns its two values with the first greater than the second and ax.xaxis_inverted() == True. Normal ascending calls (first argument < second) still yield a non-inverted ascending interval.

When an interactive (interactive=True) vertical SpanSelector is created, the two initial edge-handle artist lines are placed at data y-positions equal to the axes' current y-axis data limits (ax.get_ybound()), rather than at the initially-zero selector extents; consequently constructing the selector leaves the axes' y view limits unchanged (does not autoscale them, in particular does not expand them toward data coordinate 0 when 0 lies outside the data view).

UnitData.update invoked with empty data does not emit the INFO-level log message 'Using categorical units to plot a list of strings that are all parsable as floats or dates...' (the message is suppressed when data is empty even though the all-convertible check is vacuously true).

When a Figure is pickled via __getstate__, the dpi value stored in the resulting pickled state under the '_dpi' key is the figure's original dpi (the '_original_dpi' recorded on its canvas when it was created) rather than the figure's current, possibly device-pixel-ratio-inflated dpi; consequently any inflation of the figure's dpi caused by HiDPI/Retina device-pixel-ratio scaling is discarded on pickling and not carried into the unpickled figure.

The align grouping in _get_aligned_offsets now pairs 'left' with 'bottom' (both on the offsets=[d,...] / descent-side branch) and 'right' with 'top' (both on the offsets=[height-h+d,...] branch), so that align='top' behaves like align='right' and align='bottom' behaves like align='left' within the shared helper.

When the keep_attrs argument of Variable.quantile is left at its default (None/omitted), whether or not the result retains the calling Variable's attrs is governed by xarray's global 'keep_attrs' option consulted via _get_keep_attrs with a default of False, mirroring the behavior of other Variable reduce methods.

IndexVariable.to_index_variable() (and its to_coord alias) returns a new IndexVariable object that is distinct from the receiver rather than returning the receiver itself, so that mutating the returned variable (e.g. assigning its dims) does not change the dims of the IndexVariable it was called on.

When Dataset.set_index builds a new (multi-)index that supersedes an existing index, a coordinate variable belonging to the pre-existing (now-dropped) index — provided it is not among the variables being newly indexed and not itself recreated as one of the new index variables — is re-added to the resulting dataset as a regular de-indexed variable (via to_base_variable) instead of being removed from _variables, so no coordinate is silently deleted and referenced-coordinate integrity is preserved.

When PandasMultiIndexingAdapter.__array__ is called on an adapter whose level is set (not None), the returned numpy array is np.asarray(level_values.values, dtype=dtype) where dtype is the requested dtype argument if one was given, or otherwise the adapter's recorded dtype (self.dtype) — so the result has the requested dtype when one is supplied and otherwise preserves the recorded original level-coordinate dtype rather than whatever dtype pandas' get_level_values would otherwise produce (i.e., an int32 level coordinate is not upcast to int64).

Calling Similar.run() on an instance whose min_lines equals 0 returns immediately and does no similarity computation and produces no similarity report output on stdout (neither computed duplicates nor the TOTAL-lines summary line). Positive min_lines values still compute and display the report as before.

Calling _is_ignored_file(element, ignore_list, ignore_list_re, ignore_list_paths_re) returns True iff os.path.basename(element) is a member of ignore_list, or os.path.basename(element) matches (re.match) any pattern in ignore_list_re, or the full element path matches any pattern in ignore_list_paths_re; otherwise returns False.
pylint.modify_sys_path() additionally removes the then-current first element of sys.path when the environment variable PYTHONPATH starts with ':' and PYTHONPATH is not exactly ':'+cwd or ':.'.

When get_unpacked_marks is called on a class with consider_mro=False, it returns only the marks declared directly on that class (its own pytestmark in its __dict__) and excludes any marks inherited from super-classes.

When a RidgeClassifierCV is constructed with both cv set to a non-None value and store_cv_values=True, calling fit(X, y) raises a ValueError indicating that cv!=None and store_cv_values=True are incompatible.

In StratifiedKFold._make_test_folds, self.random_state is normalized through check_random_state into a concrete random number generator exactly once before any per-class split is produced; that single generator (whose state advances) is shared by the per-class KFold splitting kernels. As a result, for shuffle=True with an integer random_state, the shuffling of different classes comes from successive draws of the one seed-derived stream rather than each class independently re-seeding and re-deriving an identical permutation from the integer.

IterativeImputer's constructor accepts a keyword-only parameter `fill_value` that defaults to `None`, and the value passed is stored in the estimator's `fill_value` attribute, so that e.g. `IterativeImputer(fill_value=X).fill_value == X` and `get_params()` exposes it as such.

When data_to_wrap is already a pandas DataFrame, _wrap_in_pandas_container ignores the index argument and preserves the input DataFrame's own existing index; it never reassigns data_to_wrap.index from the index parameter for DataFrame inputs. Consequently it does not raise a pandas 'Length mismatch' ValueError even when the supplied index is shorter/different in length from the DataFrame's rows. (Columns are still assigned in place when the columns argument is not None.)

IsolationForest.score_samples still behaves as before for external callers: it validates the user-supplied X (accepting/ converting to float32 csr via _validate_data with reset=False) and returns the negation of the per-sample averaged anomaly scores, delegating the fitted-state check and scoring computation to an internal method that does not re-run input validation (so calling score_samples on an already-fitted DataFrame still yields the expected scores).

roc_curve returns a `thresholds` array whose first element (the extra point added so the curve starts at fpr=0, tpr=0) is exactly `np.inf`, regardless of the values or magnitude of `y_score` (e.g. even when all scores are probabilities within [0,1], thresholds[0] is inf rather than max(y_score)+1, which was previously > 1 for fraction-scale scores).

A :glob: toctree pattern never adds a std-generated special page (genindex/modindex/search or any docname whose name coincides with a std label key) as a toctree entry/includefile, even when the glob pattern nominally matches that name.

In prepend_prolog, the set of leading content lines classified as the document's docinfo region (the lines after which the rst_prolog is inserted) is determined by matching each line against docutils' genuine field-list field-marker syntax (e.g. `:Field name: value`), rather than by the presence of any `:\w+:` token in the line. Concretely, while scanning from the top of `content`, a line advances `pos` (the prolog insertion index) only if that line is an actual field-marker entry; a heading or body line that merely contains an inline interpreted-text role form such as `:mod:\`title\`` inside its text is NOT treated as docinfo, so the prolog is inserted before it rather than after its role token.

The source text argument delivered to a 'source-read' handler for included RST content is the included file's actual content — its lines joined with ' ' — excluding the two trailing marker/sentinel lines that docutils (>=0.18) appends to the include input; after the handler returns, the possibly-modified text is re-split into lines and those two marker lines are re-attached so that parsing of the included content continues identically to before the handler ran.

The std domain's ':term:' cross-reference role no longer lowercases its reference text before use, so the term reference target stored on the pending_xref node (and matched against registered glossary terms) preserves the exact capitalization written in the reference instead of being case-folded.

In _skip_member, when a class or exception member whose __qualname__ owner part is a single name (dot-free cls_path) that resolves through the equivalent of a functools.wraps wrapper, the owner-class is looked up in the module globals of the original unwrapped member object rather than the wrapper. Concretely observable: _skip_member returns False (does not skip) for such a functools.wraps-decorated __init__ that has a docstring and is owned by a single-segment class name when napoleon_include_init_with_doc is enabled — i.e. owner detection no longer fails merely because the wrapper's own __globals__ lacks the class name, so the init-with-doc inclusion decision is applied consistently with an undecorated __init__.
Calls to sphinx.ext.autodoc.importer.get_module_members(module) now emit a RemovedInSphinx50Warning deprecation warning (while still returning the computed member list).

ModuleDocumenter.get_object_members(want_all=True) distinguishes between a module whose __all__ is absent (self.__all__ is None) and a module whose __all__ is defined but empty (a list/tuple []); the defined-but-empty case is no longer treated as if __all__ were absent. Consequently, for a module with an empty defined __all__, all module members that are not named in __all__ are marked skipped (member.skipped = True) so none of them get documented, instead of falling into the 'no __all__' branch that returns all members with module-attribute checking enabled.

sphinx.ext.viewcode.collect_pages yields no viewcode pages (no per-module highlighted source pages and no '_modules/index' overview page) when the active builder is the singlehtml builder (builder.name == 'singlehtml').

For a class documented under an alias name (doc_as_attr), ClassDocumenter.get_doc returns an empty (non-None) docstring list when the class's real module source contains a module variable doc-comment for the alias name, and returns None when no such source comment exists. Consequently the alias is subjected to docstring processing (inherited autodoc-processing/autodoc-process-docstring applies to an empty docstring) only in the commented case, while an uncommented class alias still yields None and so performs no docstring processing.
For any non-empty input x, is_path_or_empty(x) validates x exactly as is_path does: it returns the (tilde-expanded) path if x resolves to an existing directory, and raises ValidationError otherwise.
The py:property directive accepts a ':classmethod:' flag option; providing it does not raise an unknown-option error.

Mock classes carry an explicit class-level __name__: a bare _MockObject instance exposes __name__ == '' (H0), while every subclass manufactured by _make_subclass (as returned by e.g. __getattr__/__getitem__ attribute access on a mock module or object, and used when a mocked class is used as a base) exposes __name__ equal to that member/attribute name (H2). Reading __name__ on a mock thus yields a real string value rather than falling back into __getattr__ and returning another mock.

In the described-only/typehints-description-target merge path (augment_descriptions_with_types), a docutils field whose extracted name is ':returns:' (parts[0] == 'returns') is recognized as describing the function's return value, exactly as a ':return:' field is.

When either the required extension version or the loaded extension's declared version is not a valid PEP 440 version string (packaging.version.Version raises InvalidVersion), verify_needs_extensions falls back to plain (lexicographic) string comparison between the required and loaded version strings to decide whether the requirement is met, raising a VersionRequirementError iff the required string is lexicographically greater than the loaded string.

Identity._entry(i, j) returns the KroneckerDelta(i, j) expression (left unevaluated) rather than a concrete scalar when Eq(i, j) evaluates to neither the boolean True object nor the boolean False object — i.e. when the indices are distinct symbolic/index expressions whose equality is not statically decidable (e.g. two independent symbols that could still be equal in value).

When Product._eval_product is applied to a term that is an Add whose as_numer_denom() yields a purely numeric (is_Number) denominator q — i.e. the term cannot be factored into independently-evaluable numerator/denominator products, such as n + 2**(-k) or n**(2/3) + 1 — the returned value is exp(Sum(log(p), (k, a, n))) / q (p being the numerator), rather than the sum over the separately-evaluated products of the numerator's individual Add addends.

In the generic Set._complement method, when the minuend argument (`other`) is a FiniteSet, elements of that FiniteSet for which the subtrahend (`self`) reports definitive containment (`self.contains(el)` evaluates to true) are removed from the result; elements the subtrahend reports as definitively-not-contained (`self.contains(el)` evaluates to false) are retained and constitute the ordinary FiniteSet members of the returned set.
polylog(0, z) auto-evaluates to z/(1 - z) for any z for which it is not already caught by the z=1, z=-1, or z=0 branches.

A bareiss pivot-candidate entry that is still non-zero (i.e. not recognizably zero after expand_mul, such as an unevaluated bare symbol or float) continues to be selectable as a pivot exactly as when the topmost truthy element was the only choice, so symbolic determinant computations that legitimately used a non-zero pivot still proceed and return a determinant (not zero) — the change only alters the handling of entries that expand to zero.

When tensor_product_simp is applied to a Mul whose sole non-commutative factor is a Pow whose base is a TensorProduct (possibly multiplied by commutative scalars), it returns the scalar multiplier times a TensorProduct in which the exponent is distributed into each argument, instead of returning the Mul unchanged.

When the first factor of a MatMul being LaTeX-printed is a negative number, output is a leading '-' followed by the space-joined rendering of the product obtained by using the absolute value of that coefficient with the remaining factors, so the negative coefficient is pulled out as a unary minus (e.g. MatMul(-1, A, B) renders as '-A B' rather than '-1 A B').

Left multiplication of a Point by a scalar factor (`factor * point`) yields a new Point whose coordinates are each the factor multiplied by the corresponding coordinate of `point`, sympified and simplified (i.e. behaves exactly the same as the corresponding right multiplication `point * factor`), rather than falling through to a generic SymPy Mul expression.

nthroot_mod(a, n, p) no longer raises NotImplementedError for composite (non-prime) modulus p with n != 2; instead it returns the sorted list of all distinct solutions x in [0, p) to x**n ≡ a (mod p), regardless of the all_roots flag.

Expression.__bool__ (truthiness of an EX ring element) returns falsy (False) whenever the wrapped SymPy expression f.ex is definitively zero, i.e. f.ex.is_zero is True, even when f.ex is not structurally equal to the Python integer 0; it returns truthy (True) in every other case (definitive nonzero or undecidable zero-ness).

Declaring __slots__=() on the Printable mixin renders instances of Printable's slot-declaring subclasses (previously, since Printable lacked __slots__, any class whose MRO passed through Printable implicitly gained an instance __dict__) __slots__-only: a Symbol instance (and any instance of a Printable-derived class that itself defines __slots__) has no instance __dict__ — accessing its __dict__ either returns absent/raises AttributeError, and assigning a new, non-slot attribute to such an instance raises AttributeError rather than silently storing it in a __dict__.

The zeros of the imaginary part im used to identify real members of an ImageSet are computed from the factors of numer(im) (the numerator when im is treated as a rational expression), so that real-valued members correspond to roots of that numerator; a purely rational/fractional form of im is reduced by its numerator rather than treated by its compounded-as-given factors.

When itermonomials is called in the integer (total-degree) form with any non-commutative variable present, a candidate monomial is yielded iff its total degree (the sum over its variable factors of their exponents) is at least min_degree — i.e. retained on the summed per-variable exponents rather than on whether any individual variable's exponent reaches min_degree.

AntiSymmetricTensor._latex renders as a brace-group enclosing the whole symbol with both its upper and lower indices, i.e. it returns '{%s^{%s}_{%s}}' formatting '{symbol^{upper}_{lower}}' rather than 'symbol^{upper}_{lower}'.
